bonuses that grant extra abilities
18 levels in the beta
notes: An XNA 4.0 / .NET 4.0 Xonix-style game. It is an 'In development', name-your-own-price beta on itch.io; the download is Cosmonix_Beta_1_04_10_2016.zip. The page links a Steam Greenlight listing. English and Russian; keyboard, mouse and Xbox controller. No full Steam release was found.

title: Pretty Girls Panic!
publisher: Zoo Corporation (PC); Eastasiasoft (consoles); Sticky Rice Games (Android)
mechanics: a water-filled barrier hides the girl; remove 75% or more of it to clear
the edge is normally safe, but crab enemies can catch the player there
an enemy touching the tool or the cut line costs a tool (life); enemies grow stronger stage by stage
bigger cut pieces score more points
13 girls over 50 stages; the girls undress gradually, with no nudity in the Steam version
each cleared stage adds a photo to a gallery; Steam leaderboards
notes: Steam release 20 Dec 2016 (Wikipedia gives 19 Dec). Console ports followed on 26 Aug 2021 via Eastasiasoft, and the game is in Pretty Girls Game Collection (Switch/PS4 physical). Wikipedia's Gals Panic article lists it among Gals Panic clones. The Android listing Wikipedia cites (com.stickyricegames.panic) now returns 404.

title: Frontiers.io
mechanics: single life: you die if anyone, including you, crosses your trail before the area is enclosed
steal land by running through opponents' territory and closing it off
destroying opponents yields gems; selectable heroes for your profile
notes: Paid ($1.99) Steam game released Oct 12, 2017, tagged Single-player only despite the .io name; the store does not say whether opponents are bots.

title: Quirky Crook
mechanics: you play a crook grabbing bags of money while cops chase you
high-score play with a score multiplier to push up
per a user review, the player moves along borders, and leaving a border can kill you (details unclear)
notes: Released 26 March 2018 as the second game in the developer's series of small, quickly made games. The store says it 'takes the best of arcade classics Qix and Snake' but does not say how, and a 2018 user review compares it to JezzBall. How capture works could not be confirmed.

title: Bishoujo Battle Cyber Panic!
mechanics: remove 75% of a 'communications barrier' to rescue each girl
clearing larger areas faster scores more
enemies are bugs and computer viruses
40 regular stages plus 10 special stages showing alternate costumes; rescued characters go to a gallery
notes: Steam release 18 Jun 2020. Steam lists nudity/sexual-content descriptors. Sold alone or in Zoo's Bishoujo Battle bundle.

title: Delta Light
mechanics: fruit pickups give stackable stat boosts (Cherries for super speed, Melons for toughness)
11 unlockable characters (10 plus 1 added in v1.1), each with a passive effect, switchable per map
Infinite mode (v1.1): pseudo-randomly generated maps with affixes and a rank-up system
level editor whose maps are shared as a text string
75+ campaign maps
notes: Steam release Nov 9, 2020. The player is a ghost named Delta who draws lines to remove parts of the field. The 'qix' and 'pacman' tags are on the sequel's itch.io page; no itch.io page was found for this first game.

title: Get Your Klix on Route 66
mechanics: the roaming Qix-like KLIX is a Route 66-sign-shaped beast, different in each of 12 cities from Chicago to Los Angeles
HAX road-sign hazards and BRIX police-officer enemies
blue BRIX trap the player and erase drawn lines; CTRL-X self-destructs to escape a trap
no lives: start with 10,000 points and lose escalating points per death
claim more than each level's stated threshold to advance
notes: Made in Construct; full Windows game $3. No date on the page; the year is inferred from the itch page id (751487), which falls between pages published in mid-2020.

title: Magical Stock Princess
mechanics: Gals Panic-inspired action stages: clear the floor while avoiding monsters
action stages alternate with adventure stages with light RPG elements and character interaction
collecting food is the run's core goal
saves are not free: they are earned by completing mini-quests
three endings plus a special bad ending; secrets and references
notes: Steam release 21 Jul 2020. A hybrid of area-clear arcade and adventure game.

title: Pretty Girls Panic! PLUS
mechanics: choose a partner (Yu or Asahi); clearing stages with her raises friendship and unlocks partner costumes
enemies have attacks to dodge, not only bodies
clear by securing a set percentage of the area; each stage also unlocks special costumes
40 stages; 22 voiced characters; gallery; Steam leaderboards
notes: An improved version of Pretty Girls Panic!. Steam release 9 Mar 2021 (Wikipedia gives 10 Mar). Consoles followed on 4 Nov 2021, and the game is in Pretty Girls Game Collection II.

title: Fillit
mechanics: competitive local multiplayer: up to 4 players claim territory in the same arena on one screen (PvP)
40+ two-player local co-op levels
power-ups that affect all players and can disrupt opponents
90+ single-player levels whose new enemies attack from all directions
notes: Released 2 June 2022 on Steam for $1.99. The store says it is inspired by Xonix and Volfied. Steam tags include 4 Player Local, Competitive, Local Co-Op and Physics. It is not the 2000s browser game 'Fill It' that the 2007 Wikipedia Qix article and the Qixote wiki ('Fill It!') mention. That is a different, older game.

title: JezzBall Atomic
mechanics: Classic mode keeps the original rules and chamber size
Arcade mode: 40 levels in much larger chambers, with Jezz atom types that each behave differently
Survival mode: start with 10 lives and gain 1 at the start of each level
notes: Released on Steam on 14 Feb 2022. A remake of the Windows Entertainment Pack's JezzBall.

title: Xonix Casual Edition
mechanics: 3D Xonix in which the player flies a copter that leaves a trail of straight lines
enemy drones with different abilities roam the field; hitting a drone, having a drone hit your trail, or crossing your own trail ends the attempt
each level has about a one-minute time limit, which bonuses can extend
pickups: speed boost, enemy slower, coins, extra time and extra life; some pickups are harmful
90 levels with unique layouts and rising difficulty
notes: A 3D Xonix sold on Steam (released 25 Aug 2023) and on itch.io (where buying includes a Steam key). Localized in English, Russian, French, Spanish, Arabic and Portuguese. The itch.io page mentions mobile optimization, but only a Windows release was found.

title: Gensou -Yumegokochi- Illusion -Dreamlike-
mechanics: HP and defence, upgraded with money collected each stage, replace one-hit deaths
Unrivaled Barrier: a temporary shield ability
Transcendence Mode: fast, invincible free movement for a time
enemies fire waves of attacks that must be dodged while drawing
no item power-ups and no time limit
114 stages including hidden ones; post-game HELL Mode (attacks cannot be blocked) and Boss Rush
Bullet Hell mode (Mar 2026 update): about 5x enemy attacks, timed race to a 100% clear
clearing a stage above a quota unlocks a timed 'tawamure' touch mode with the stage's yokai character (Japan/Asia builds; free patch for Steam and Epic; absent from Western Switch)
notes: Debut title of a Sendai studio. Nintendo eShop (Japan) Nov 22, 2024; Western Switch and Epic around Oct 2025; Steam Nov 20, 2025. Story: as the head of a shrine you travel the six Tohoku prefectures freeing corrupted yokai. DLC characters were added later.

title: Delta Light 2
mechanics: 35+ handcrafted campaign maps, nearly each introducing new mob types, with many bosses
visual-novel segments between stages
7 unlockable characters with passive abilities and distinct playstyles
stackable fruit stat boosts (Cherries, Melons, Bananas and more)
after the campaign, a mostly procedural Infinite Mode seeded by the player's Steam ID
Arcade Mode (patch 1.13): no story, nothing saved, aimed at cabinets and speedrunners
notes: Steam release Mar 19, 2025; free demo on itch.io May 28, 2025. itch.io tags include qix and pacman; the page states no generative AI was used. Line-drawing rules and stage goals are not detailed.

title: Jezzball Classic Deluxe Edition
mechanics: points awarded for each enclosed area, with a leaderboard to climb (the page gives no details)
notes: Released on Steam on 26 Feb 2025 at $12.99, with pixel-style levels. Otherwise a straight clone: 75% goal within a time limit, lives equal the atom count, one atom added per level, left-click to place a wall and right-click to change its direction.

title: LiM Grid Wars
mechanics: alien ships hunt the player while you claim area (Qix-style lines drawn from the border, shown in store screenshots)
temporary upgrades shown in an 'Active Bonus' panel
enemy AI said to adapt to your moves
conquer target rises per level (55% on level 1, 75% on level 5 in screenshots); capturing beyond the target is allowed
10 levels of rising difficulty with a high-score table
notes: Released 14 Aug 2025 on Steam, $9.99, Windows only. The store text never mentions lines, but the screenshots show classic Qix play: trails cut from the border, a claimed-area % against a 'To conquer' target, lives, and enemies on the claimed edge. Developer looks Swedish (in a 'Made in Norrbotten' bundle).

title: Vertex (Komodor)
mechanics: player droid moves along new or existing orthogonal lines to capture a percentage of the screen
enemy droids patrol, some predictable and some erratic; over 20 droid types
60 levels, 5 gameplay modes, 3 difficulty levels on Steam (itch page says 4)
notes: Godot. Released on Steam 14 Aug 2025 ($0.99); the itch release devlog is dated 23 Aug 2025 ($1 minimum).

title: Domain Expansion
mechanics: 3D territory capture (Steam tags: 3D, Third Person)
choose NORMAL (safer) or DEEP (riskier, higher-scoring) before each cut
enemies roam inside the board and patrol the boundary
timed acceleration and 'territory eaters' that take back captured ground
some stages also clear by separating two interior enemies
24 stages, then a second loop with a higher capture target
checkpoint continues and a local score ranking
notes: Released 3 Nov 2026 on Steam, self-published. The camera is not described; 'third person' comes from the Steam tags only.

title: Dream Snake Adventure
mechanics: cut rectangles into the arena to win territory while dodging enemies
story worlds
Create mode for building arenas, with an online browser of created levels
Local Battle against bots (local multiplayer)
Daily Challenge high-score mode
shop with head props; optional PG-16 DLC picture content
notes: Its pages say it is inspired by Qix and Gals Panic. Open beta (v0.9) with a free demo at dreamsnake.app. The Game Jolt page was posted in June 2026.

title: Filltopia
mechanics: turn-based: tap a trigger button to extend a wall to the next obstacle; the enclosed area fills with the current player's color, then the turn passes
whoever has the largest colored area at the end wins
hazards: walking bombs, flying mines and UFOs
local multiplayer on one device (vs the computer or 'up to 4 friends')
over 99 handcrafted levels plus computer-generated levels
notes: Released on Steam on 12 Mar 2026 at $5.99. A turn-based competitive take on wall-splitting. Steam discloses AI-assisted background art.

title: Glowfield
mechanics: anything that touches the open trail breaks it
captures reveal glowing pictures: 31 across 5 worlds, kept in a gallery
short levels with instant retry; three stars per level
powers: dash along your trail, snare an enemy in a pocket of light, shield, seeds of light (extra time and a freeze), Nova, hold-to-focus slow motion
enemies: Drifters, Seekers that bend toward your trail, Crawlers that move along the shore, Giants that cannot be snared, Dashers that charge
Infinity endless mode: rising difficulty, lives carry over, top-10 hi-scores
local multiplayer: Two Sparks co-op, Claim War (two tints, more light wins), Hunt (one player claims while the other steers the dark, then swap); a bot can play the second spark
notes: $2.99 minimum (pay what you want above that) with a free demo. Published 16 Oct 2026, v1.0.0, Windows 10/11 64-bit. AI-assisted. Cites Qix and JezzBall. The asymmetric Hunt mode is the notable twist.

title: In My Imagination
mechanics: after a cut, only enclosed areas with no monster inside become territory
the player can reposition through already-claimed territory
releasing the draw button retraces your path at double speed; you cannot turn during the retrace and can still be hit
monster patterns: drifting, chasing your trail, signaled turns, charged dashes, route patrols
Normal mode: reveal 85% within a time limit with 3 lives; a no-damage clear records your fastest flawless time
Area Challenge: past 85% the run continues until a single hit, aiming for the highest percentage
Endless Dreams: random collected images at 3 minutes each, auto-advance at 85%, 3 shared lives, monsters rising to ten
70 image stages; Dream Gallery
notes: The Steam page lists release on 12 Nov 2026 (not yet out on 9 Nov 2026). The developer discloses generative-AI use for some illustrations and assets. Suggestive swimwear art.

title: Line Fight
mechanics: touching any line, yours or a rival's, eliminates you
4 monsters, from a wandering bouncer to a pathfinding boss that targets your unfinished line; touching a monster or its line is fatal, but monsters can be trapped or blown up
7 items (Stealth, Jump, Freeze, Mine, Revive, Speed, Double); some lie on the map, others are hidden in land and gained when it is claimed
rivals can be forced into your line or trapped inside your territory
19 shaped maps (star, heart, gear, crescent) whose outlines change how claiming works
online 4/6/8-player matches with bots filling empty seats; private rooms by 6-digit code; ranked play with 7 tiers and 28-day seasons
notes: Items hidden under unclaimed land are a reward-for-capture idea. The developer discloses AI-generated elements in the icon, background and promotional media.

title: Paper IO Game
mechanics: start from a small base and claim empty space by looping a trail back to it; the trail is vulnerable outside the safe zone and one hit eliminates you
real-time online play: the listing declares server-based networked multiplayer
notes: Straight Paper.io clone sold for USD 10 on itch.io (tagline 'Mark your path, steal the world'). Made with Phaser; keyboard and mouse input. The page shows no date; the year is inferred from its itch.io project ID (4480071, which falls between projects dated February and June 2026).

title: point line surface
mechanics: the character moves only along its own network of drawn lines
line segments are a resource: collect energy to earn new segments
a line that reconnects to your territory captures the enclosed area
ranged shooting (manual or auto) and a grab hook that pulls certain enemies in to capture and absorb them
absorbing enemies drives a card-based level-up system
enemies keep entering and new types appear as territory grows; the run ends if territory is destroyed or HP runs out
a mid-run boss must be beaten before you can safely expand
permanent meta upgrades between runs; planned: a Hex Shop where line segments buy rule mutators, and a 'Car Legion' of recruited captured enemies
notes: Roguelite Qix-like in which line length is a spendable resource. Early Access from 10 Sep 2026 at $2.99; the vertical slice has 4 stages, 19 waves and 10 enemy types.

title: RPG Maker MZ Territory Action Plugin
alt_titles: 【RPGツクールMZ】陣取りアクションプラグイン
mechanics: FAST and SLOW drawing, each with its own speed and score value
the side of the cut without enemies is claimed
field enemies with configurable chase strength, random turns and speed changes; border enemies chase the player along the safe edge
field enemies fire bullets, including 3-way and 5-way spreads and shots that ricochet off borders
items that spawn over time, on capture or at fixed spots: speed up, extra life, score, timed invincibility
hidden illustration revealed region by region; per-stage clear percentage
bonus score for area claimed beyond the clear threshold
on-screen virtual controller for touch and browser play
notes: Released 25 Aug 2026 for 550 yen (DLsite category: tools/accessories). Comes with a HUD plugin, a stage-tag generator and a sample project. Works on normal MZ maps.

title: Rusty Robot Wants to Cry
mechanics: 100+ levels whose rules switch between platforming, digging, dodging, bouncing and Xonix-style territory claiming (remixes Arkanoid, Xonix, Digger and Snake)
every level's goal is to grab the key and reach the door
glitch bosses that you sometimes fight and sometimes need help from
three stars per level for collecting everything
notes: Upcoming on Steam (Windows only per the Steam API). Territory capture is one rule set among several arcade mechanics, not the core of every level. Chiptune music is generated on the fly.

title: Stake That Claim
mechanics: two line speeds: a quick line escapes danger, a careful line earns triple territory points
rivals that reach your unfinished line cut it
clear by claiming 75% or by splitting the rival balls into separate areas
20 rival ball types with different movement, mixed in new combinations as you progress
extra lives and bonuses; results screen with time bonus and combo multiplier
3D stadium presentation with crowd, cheerleaders and announcer reacting to big moves
notes: Single-player against computer-controlled rivals. Sold on itch.io ($4.99) and the Mac App Store ($2.99), with Game Center achievements and a global leaderboard. No exact release date is shown; the site copyright is 2026. AI-assisted per the itch disclosure.

title: TERR1T0RY
publisher: Mutant Shark (self-published on itch.io, account enkeria)
mechanics: hazards: bouncing spikes, erratic triangles, precision lasers, chompers
power-ups: speed boost, time slowdown, Green Blast Mines, board-clearing chomper wipe
risk-reward bonus points for near-miss evasions, defusing timed bombs, and large single captures
completing stages reveals retrowave background art
15 levels with dynamic hazard spawns; Timed Trial mode alongside classic progression
notes: Godot. Published 26 Oct 2026. Name-your-own-price in the browser; the Windows download costs $2 minimum. Has a CRT shader and gamepad support.

title: TERRITORY SCRAMBLE
mechanics: hex tiles are claimed simply by stepping on them, not by drawing a trail
a closed loop of your team's tiles captures every tile inside it at once (option, can be switched off)
shooter layer: machine guns, shotguns, mines, and plasma cannons whose shots pass through obstacles
pickups: healing, armor, speed, and a radar that shares intel with the team
enemy bases are respawn points that can be captured; Base Capture mode is won by taking every base
capturable cannons whose shells claim the tiles they hit
team play: up to 16 players online in 2-4 teams; solo or co-op against AI teams with Easy/Normal/Hard bots
match length selectable at 1, 3, 5, 7 or 10 minutes; three map layouts, toggleable obstacles, items, enclosure capture, bases and cannons
notes: Top-down team shooter on Steam built around tile and enclosure capture. Not a browser .io game: a paid Steam title, so recategorised as indie-commercial.

title: Tint Turf
mechanics: paint a loop off your turf and return to claim it; any opponent crossing your wet trail knocks you out
story mode 'Wet Paint Wars': a five-job campaign against rival bot crews (Smudge, Drip, Rollo)
modes: 90-second Turf War (most turf wins), endless Free Paint, Daily arena with pillars and a 150-second clock
unlocks: Drop Cloth (survives the first cut each round), Turbo Roller, larger starting lot, mint and gold paints
notes: $2.99 minimum, single-player against bot crews, no account needed. The developer discloses AI assistance for code, graphics, sounds and text.

title: Unveil (Qix-style picture reveal plugin)
alt_titles: Unveil - Qix-Style Picture Reveal Minigame for RPG Maker MZ
Unveil - Reveal Any Picture, a Qix-Style Minigame for GameMaker
mechanics: configurable 1-4 field creatures and 0-6 edge sparks, target share (10-95% in the GameMaker version) and lives
closing a cut claims every creature-free region at once

veil materials drawn in code over any picture (3 in MZ, 8 in GameMaker)

scripted input supported for tutorials and replays (GameMaker version)

title: VoidMania
mechanics: fuse: an enemy touching your open line lights a fuse that burns toward you; hold SPACE to retrace to safety before it arrives or lose a life

boss attacks: hunting, bullet spreads, teleporting, splitting, serpent bodies, tentacle sweeps, minion hatching, beams across the field
21 enemy behaviours, including hunters that come for you as soon as a line starts, wall crawlers, orbiters, zigzaggers, wanderers, mine layers, pulsing speeders and dividers
power-up crate per level with 10 power-up types, including speed, shield, freeze, laser, slow-mo, 2x score and bombs
4 sector modifiers: fog, rush, mirror, dark void
chain multiplier for captures made in quick succession
three stars per level: clear, claim a high percentage or trap the boss, and finish without dying
claimed territory reveals a hidden picture
modes: 48-level campaign over 8 sectors, endless, daily challenge with a shared seed, time attack on cleared levels
synthwave soundtrack intensifies while an enemy has touched your open line

The Steam page lists achievements and leaderboards. The star threshold is given as both 90% and 80% on Steam, so it is unclear. The itch page shows no publish date (only 'updated 19 days ago').

title: Warix
mechanics: 1v1 top-down twin-stick fighter: leave your base to draw a trail, return to enclose and claim area

instant win at 50% of the map
combat layer: shoot bullets or melee swipe; a well-timed swipe parries bullets in flight
glowing spores, driven over or enclosed in captured turf, fill an energy ring; boost spends it to dodge, expand faster or chase
online private and quick matches, plus training vs AI (Easy, Normal, Beast Mode)
notes: Not yet released; a demo is available on Steam. Electron-microscope look with fluid shaders and CRT glitches on hit.

title: Gal Pani X
mechanics: each stage starts in a randomly sized claimed rectangle at the centre and expands outward; the player moves freely inside claimed land instead of being locked to edges

Most pictures show To Heart characters: suggestive and NSFW, but no nudity. GOG Dreamlist also notes diagonal movement. Wikipedia's Gals Panic article lists it among clones but wrongly credits it to 'To Heart'.

title: Tetrangle
mechanics: areas cut out of the field become blocks
the blocks are stacked Tetris-style to score points
notes: Japanese freeware described as 'like Qix and Tetris combined, retro style'. Version 0.1, file dated 10 Feb 2012.

title: Boxer (lowrezjam)
mechanics: very low-resolution playfield (made under #lowrezjam's pixel limit)
notes: Made for #lowrezjam in May 2014 and published on Game Jolt on 1 Jun 2014. The author calls it a clone of an unnamed childhood game 'of which JezzBall is also a clone'. Game Jolt gives no rules.

title: CYBER FIELD-K
mechanics: five stages with branching routes; about 20 minutes per full run
Ver 2.00 'Re-Boost' update adds a Boost Mode and rebalances for easier play
notes: Japanese freeware territory-capture (陣取り) action game starring Pronama-chan (Kurei Kei), mascot of the 'Programming Nama Housou' community, who fights viruses in cyberspace with a self-made defence program. Freem! says it will remind players of Qix and Volfied. Registered on Freem! on 2014-11-17; current version 2.10 (updated 2021-09-27); runs on Windows XP/7/8/10.

title: xXIXx
mechanics: win target lowered to 30% of the screen
notes: 'Homage to QIX', made for #awkwardjam. Published 24 Feb 2015.

title: Bunnyix
mechanics: 3D presentation of arcade Qix, played with keyboard and mouse
notes: The page says only that it is a 3D clone of the arcade game Qix, made for a game jam that is not named. It is name-your-price (free) and tagged 3D, Arcade, Puzzle and Vector. The year is estimated from its low itch.io game id (92171, below Doki Doki Literature Club's 106599 from 2017).

title: Love Me
mechanics: slash 'bad' objects Fruit Ninja-style and circle 'good' ones Qix-style
short (5-6 minute) narrative about self-worth framed by positive psychology
notes: "Fruit Ninja meets Qix and positive psychology". Name-your-price. The page describes no further mechanics. The year is estimated from the itch.io game id (316523).

title: Qix (alobker, Ludum Dare 42)
notes: Straight clone made for Ludum Dare 42 (theme 'Running out of space'), published 12 Aug 2018. No rule changes from Qix are documented.

title: Xonitix
mechanics: one-dimensional Xonix: claim space on a single terminal line while avoiding moving dots
ASCII text-mode presentation
notes: Made for Terminal Jam 2018 in C++ with no extra libraries. Version 2 builds dated 11 Nov 2018. MIT-licensed source on GitHub (garu/Xonitix).

title: Conquerors
mechanics: two bugs start from small corner bases and leave trails; looping back to their own land fills the enclosed area (Paper.io-style)
local 2-player on one keyboard (WASD vs arrow keys) with per-player area counters and a round timer
notes: Free Windows download (conquerors.exe). The text says only that two bugs try to capture as much territory as they can; the capture rule above comes from the page screenshots. The page shows no date; the year is inferred from its itch.io project ID (513592, between projects dated April 2019 and January 2020).

title: Nova Xonix 3D
year: 2019 or earlier (earliest dated item: devlog of 12 Jan 2019)
mechanics: 3D-rendered Xonix flown with a hi-tech flying craft
bonuses that can help or harm
notes: A free, name-your-own-price 3D Xonix remake. Its itch.io tags include air-xonix-3d, which suggests it follows AirXonix.

title: Tablix
mechanics: the boss ('big bad') spawns green balls; capturing a green ball switches you to colour paint
two-tier scoring: white paint 1 point per square, colour paint 2 points per square
win at 75% or more painted
notes: Paint Jam 2020 entry (3-5 Apr 2020; art made in MS Paint), name-your-own-price.

title: Virtual Bug Catcher
mechanics: enclosing 'bugs' inside the red safe zone removes them for good
direct contact with a bug 'crashes' the software (game over)
endless play (tagged Endless)
notes: Made in Godot in about three days as a deliberately cheap Qix clone for the 'So Bad it's Good' Jam 2020. A devlog is dated 26 Jun 2020.

title: J-Ball 2021
publisher: Newbie Indie Game Dev (self-published on itch.io, name your own price)
mechanics: faithful JezzBall remake: left-click starts a wall at the pointer, right-click rotates the next wall, capture 75% to clear
notes: Made with Unity, mouse-only and textless. The page shows no publish date. The year comes from the title and a '5 years ago' comment (as of Nov 2026). The page links a video devlog about how it was made.

title: Metal Stuck
mechanics: captured areas reveal artwork by Berlin underground graphic designers from STUCK magazine, drawn in DOS-era pixel art
after the large monsters are defeated, the player can keep uncovering the artwork at their own pace with no threat
notes: A homage to DOS Volfied, made during an MA in Berlin in collaboration with STUCK magazine. itch.io marks it as in development. The Game Jolt page (described as 'Volfied clone', made in Stencyl) was posted in November 2020 and published on 2021-03-27, so the two listings appear to be the same game.

title: The Last Plast
notes: A free claymation Xonix remake, made as a Bezalel 'Indie Studio' student project, with animation by Omri Lechnik. Tagged volfied and xonix. The page does not describe the rules.

title: Spherical Qix
mechanics: playfield projected onto a shaded sphere; drag to rotate the view
reveal a target percentage of the surface before time runs out
enemies only interfere while you draw, and only set you back a bit (no lives)
HUD sits on the back of the sphere, so you rotate it to read progress
notes: Devlog 'Qix reshaped' dated 16 Feb 2022; status on hold. The developer planned a life count and a boss. Uses WASD or an on-screen touch pad.

title: Tinnitus
mechanics: 3D levels (tagged 'cube'); fill 80% of each level by reaching the blue or grey safe zones
an enemy touching your path while you build makes it decay quickly; reach a safe zone before it vanishes or restart the level
notes: A tribute to AirXonix and Qix for Finally Finish Something 2022, built in Unity in 20 days. A decaying trail replaces instant death.

title: Beaver Dam
mechanics: themed reskin: a beaver builds dams to wall off crocodile-infested water, with crocodiles in place of the Qix
the stated goal is to clear the whole map 'in one piece' rather than reach a percentage
notes: "A qix-like game" in Unity; the itch.io status is Canceled. Arrow keys or WASD. The year is estimated from the itch.io game id (2255871).

title: CuteQix
mechanics: captured area reveals AI-generated cute animal photos
30+ levels, one animal each, with 3 sub-levels showing different pictures of that animal; goals rise 60% / 70% / 80%
levels unlock in sequence; beaten levels can be replayed to view the unlocked picture
12 avatars: 4 at start, 8 unlocked through play
notes: Name-your-own-price (listed as 'Free'), v0.3 download. The developer states all images are AI-generated. Sparx and Qix enemies are as in the original. The earliest dated item is a devlog of 13 Mar 2024 announcing the free release; the itch game id (2455980) suggests the page was created around late 2023.

title: DEIFLOV
mechanics: reversed roles: enemies try to claim the playfield and the player must stop them
5-minute rounds that end when enemies reach a set claimed percentage or time runs out
score and coins earned per round buy weapons and power-ups in a shop between rounds
twin-stick-style control: WASD movement, mouse aiming, three abilities on keys 1-3
notes: A Ludum Dare 54 entry. You play Riwmoni, a native Volfiedian taking revenge on the humans who exploited the planet Volfied, which turns Volfied's story around.

title: Erix 3310
mechanics: limited to the Nokia 3310's resolution and two-colour palette
arrow keys or numpad 2/4/6/8 (phone-keypad layout)
notes: A straight clone, for NOKIA 3310 JAM 5 (devlog 23 Feb 2023), of 'Erix', the territory game on Ericsson phones that the developer played as a kid. The page names the phone 'T86i' and is tagged t68/t68i. The page describes no rules beyond controls and is tagged qix.

title: Milo's Ghosts
mechanics: ghost-house theme: the robot Milo's Blaster seals ghosts into smaller and smaller areas
score grows with the area captured
notes: An area-capture game inspired by Ambrosia's Barrack, made in Godot for Go Godot Jam 4 (5-14 May 2023). The itch.io status is 'In development'. The page does not describe controls.

title: PAINT'NT
mechanics: the player is a paintbrush, and claiming territory paints in a picture (jam special object: brush)
notes: Unity prototype for Mini Jame Gam #18 (2-4 June 2023; theme 'Can't stop moving', special object a brush), described as 'A QIX-like painti'nt game'. Jam comments say it is easy (one line can take about 40% of the field), that the enemy behaviour was unclear, and that it has no audio; one compared it to Volfied. The developer mentions a Windows build, but only HTML5 is listed.

title: Quarosel
mechanics: two-player local versus on one shared field: both players grab screen space
one button per player (Space / Enter): hold to aim, release to execute a cut
players sabotage each other with their balls and can counter an opponent's cut while it is still under way
players can be trapped in corners as the free field shrinks into a 'death pit'
notes: Ludum Dare 54 Jam entry (published on ldjam.com 2 Oct 2023), made with Godot, tagged qix and duel. The rules come only from the short LD blurb ('Greed out in a shrinking death pit of screen-estate...'); the aim-and-release cut may play closer to JezzBall than to Qix trail drawing.

title: The Zamio
mechanics: claiming at least 80% captures the whole building (level framed as a building to take over)
enemies are bugs plus larger threats
safe movement along wall edges
notes: A Global Game Jam 2023 prototype (Unity) whose page cites Qix and Volfied as inspirations. Name-your-own-price.

title: Trappy Pixel
year: 2023 (HTML5 and Mac builds announced 23 Nov 2023; Windows/Linux possibly earlier)
mechanics: enemy pixels roam the field trying to stop you; trapping them in small enclosures raises the fill
fill 75% to advance; bonus grows with fill, and 99% counts as a 'perfect' level
90-second limit per level; when it runs out more enemy pixels spawn
'Reverse' power-up reverses the enemy pixels' direction
1 player or 2 players alternating; four difficulty levels, each with its own high-score table
notes: Made in Godot and inspired by Qix, Xonix, JezzBall and Zolyx (a commenter calls it a Zolyx clone). Story: evil pixels stole the colour from Trappy's world. Gamepad supported.

title: Descaler
mechanics: Volfied-inspired shooter: the targets are cyberdragons to be 'descaled'
right click fires a grappling hook
WASD movement with mouse aiming
notes: A GMTK Game Jam 2024 entry made in two days. The authors say it is incomplete in many ways, and a commenter notes it has no music or sound effects. The page does not explain how area capture works, so how it relates to territory capture is unclear.

title: Mirror Qix
mechanics: the author describes 'rogue-like extensions' added to arcade Qix (not detailed on the page)
notes: Godot entry to Godot Wild Jam #75 (8-17 November 2024; its entries cite the theme 'Reflections', which likely explains the title). WASD controls; the Qix and the Fuze are the hazards. The page notes problems on iOS.

title: Scalar Snake
mechanics: you are a snake: enclose areas with your body to capture blocks
captured blocks increase the snake's size (jam theme 'Built to Scale')
a virus steadily eats away your captured blocks, so you must keep capturing to hold your mass
scored on three metrics: biggest captured mass, largest single capture, longest survival
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2024 entry (theme 'Built to Scale'), made in Unity in 96 hours. Jam blurb: 'Think Splix.io but a virus is eating you alive'. Ranked #409 for Enjoyment, #726 Overall.

title: Snip It!
mechanics: capturing canvas also defeats enemies (Steam: 'Draw lines to capture the canvas and defeat enemies!'; the exact rule is not described)
25 fixed levels; clearing all 25 wins the game
click/touch-to-move control as well as WASD/arrow keys
notes: Free to play on Steam, released 22 Mar 2024. Also free in the browser on itch.io (made with Phaser). Inspired by Qix and by the art-class minigame in Rockstar's Bully.

title: Xonix (hadaromer)
mechanics: player is a student fleeing 'F' (failed exam) enemies
the background behind claimed areas changes to escape locations (beaches, parties) as territory is claimed
notes: Free Unity WebGL game. The year is inferred, not stated. The page has no date, but the HTML build folder is named 'build_26_10' and the itch game id (3037135) sits just below that of another Unity Xonix remake, Idan-Shalom's, whose developer comment is dated 3 Nov 2024. That places this one in about October 2024.

title: Xonix (TheBoss2)
notes: Straight clone, described as a 'Simple take on a classic game Xonix'. Published on Game Jolt on 23 Mar 2024; made with Visual Basic; free 15 kB download.

title: XONIX 1984 2 player remake
mechanics: local 2-player versus: both players claim land at the same time and can take land the other has claimed
when the players collide, a duel starts, won by alternately mashing the left and right keys
notes: Free Unity game. Player 1 uses the arrow keys, player 2 uses A and D. The developer's comment on the page is timestamped 2024-11-03, so it was released by then. Full screen is not fully supported in the web build.

title: Blobbed Away
mechanics: crossing your own trail or moving backward along it kills you
enclosing Soots (enemies) inside a claim captures them for bonus points
Arcade mode: 3 lives; each level adds Soots and raises the area quota
Soot Hunt mode: clear by enclosing every Soot; count-up timer with best time saved per level
Time Challenge mode: one life and 60 seconds; score is the claimed percentage
notes: Released 8 July 2025, pay-what-you-want, Windows 10+, keyboard only. Themed on The Blob (player) and the soot sprites of Spirited Away (enemies). You are safe on claimed ground.

title: Demon Wreath
mechanics: turn-based puzzle (tagged Sokoban): encircle demons in salt to banish them
undo key (Z)
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 entry made in Godot; pixel-art puzzle. The page's only description is 'Encircle demons in salt to excise them from this realm.'

title: Encircle (chlowo)
mechanics: top-down bullet-hell arcade shooter where looping your path around enemies defeats them instead of shooting them
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 entry. The page gives only a one-line description ('An arcade shooter where you can loop around enemies to defeat them'), so the loop rules and controls are unknown.

title: Encircle (Cyantist)
mechanics: draw freehand loops around enemies with mouse drag or touch
each loop weakens an enemy and fills its seal gauge; a full gauge captures it, so tough enemies need several loops
the goal is to seal an unleashed phoenix from a failed summoning
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 entry made in Godot in 24 hours.

title: Enveloping Darkness
mechanics: each capture is a circular arc set by three mouse-placed control points instead of a straight line
the player is a swarm of darkness enveloping a star; getting too close to the star destroys you
capturing too much space at once is penalised
spaceships fire missiles that can hit you while you capture an arc; planets are harmless
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 entry with a post-jam devlog dated 8 August 2025; status On hold. Curved, mouse-defined captures are a rare variation.

title: Go Around
mechanics: your shots form the loop, not your movement: shoot around enemies, never at them
an enemy dies when a loop of your shots encircles it
top-down roguelike/roguelite run structure against rogue AI robots
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 entry made in raylib. Controls: WASD to move, left mouse to shoot.

title: Loopinball
mechanics: a pinball's trail is the line: loop it around bumpers to score them
blue bumpers give +5000 points and red bumpers give -5000, so loops must avoid enclosing red ones
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 entry made in Godot (programming Zunari, art Niko, music BloodPixelHero). The enclosing line is drawn by a physics-driven trail with good and bad targets.

title: Ouroboy
mechanics: the snake's body is the trail: wrap it around a herd of cows and touch your own tail tip to close the loop and capture them
crossing your own body cuts the snake instead of killing you
colliding with obstacles costs a life
clear a level by capturing every cow; six levels, the last a surprise
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 (30 July-3 August 2025, theme 'Loop') entry made in Godot; you play a snake cowboy.

title: Overheat
mechanics: a drifting car's skid trail is the capture line: close a loop to collect the blocks enclosed in it
timed score run (points with a countdown clock)
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 racing entry made in Unity. The author's whole description is 'A game about enclosing objects in your drift trail.' The timer is known only from a player comment ('230 pts with 822.37 secs left').

title: Pyrodrome
developer: Matt Chandler, Alex Norfleet, Áiron Bruce, Zachary Adams, turncoda, Tilak Devendran, Vanessa Merlis, FOUDIA (itch account chandlerm35)
mechanics: a drifting truck leaves a trail of fire; close the loop to capture the enclosed territory
drive over an opponent's trail to cut it off
driving over your own territory builds a boost meter
alternate 'Hazard Level' stage with power-ups and hazards: bomb, ice, scorcher, big mode
1v1 against the CPU, local 1v1 (two gamepads) or remote play via Parsec; most territory at round end wins
notes: Made in 96 hours for the GMTK Game Jam 2025 in Unreal Engine; listed as in development. Credits cite Splatoon, Crash Bash and Star Sled as inspirations.

title: Qixotic
mechanics: 2-player local versus on one keyboard: hoverbikes with accelerate, brake and turn controls (vehicle steering, not grid moves) leave trails; closed loops capture territory
speed boost while moving through your own territory
you may cross enemy territory, but touching the enemy's trail or crashing loses
most territory when the timer ends wins
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 entry (theme 'loop').

title: Ribix
notes: A free Brazilian-Portuguese qix-style game, released 16 Jun 2025 and made in Godot as the developer's first project (about 30 days). Inspired by 'Celebrities Hacked', whose DLC the developer could not buy. Tagged Anime, Cute and Fantasy; marked AI-assisted for graphics. The page describes no rules and does not mention a picture reveal.

title: Rodeo Rampage
mechanics: draw a lasso loop with the mouse; enclosing an animal pulls it toward you and stuns it
limited rope: a drawing longer than the cap is invalid
kick stunned animals into their matching pens to score
combos and power-ups
endless mode for as many rounds as possible; R zooms out to find animals and pens
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 entry made in Godot. The rope-length budget is a cap on trail length.

title: Schloop
mechanics: the snake encircles objects and enemies to devour them; each stage's goal is to encircle and eat a goal object
researchers will not step on slime: wall all four sides of a researcher's tile with slime or your body to stun it, then eat it to grow longer
spit can be shot in any direction, and the game turns into a shooter from level 3
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 entry, distributed as a Windows .exe zip.

title: Sewernir
mechanics: the trail is a rope that lures enemies; it attaches to wall hooks, and the loop closes only when you reattach it to the same wall side where it started
limited rope length: going too far snatches you back; the current rope can be dropped and restarted at will
floor pins anchor the rope mid-field without closing the loop
closing a loop sucks the enemies inside into a pipe, which must lie inside the loop or nothing is captured
rope length and other stats are upgraded between levels
late-game drink button triggers a special ability
notes: Ludum Dare 58 (October 2025, theme 'Collector') Compo entry made in Godot. Puzzle game inspired by Dino Master and Qix.

title: Smokescreen
mechanics: hold to lay smoke behind your ship; surrounding enemies in a smoke loop destroys them
laying smoke drains your ship's own health bar
enemies damage a mothership you must defend
time loop: your past lives replay alongside you and fight with you
escalating Vampire Survivors-inspired enemy waves, score attack; Shift to sprint
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 top-down space entry. The page does not say whether past-life ghosts also lay smoke, but replayed past runs fighting with you suggest deterministic replay ghosts.

title: Snake Loop
mechanics: circle your snake around foxes to defeat them
tongue (Space) and rattle (Right Shift) stun foxes
endless survival: last as long as possible
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 entry made in Unity.

title: Wrangler
mechanics: loop your rope to expand your territory
loop the rope around enemies to pop them
enemies touching your fragile rope kill you
two levels and a win area to reach, rather than a percentage target
notes: GMTK Game Jam 2025 entry made in Godot; cowboy-themed free-roaming Paper.io-like. Downloadable only (no browser build); WASD or arrow keys, no other buttons. The page states no generative AI was used.

title: BeastGrid
mechanics: two rule sets: Classic, quick tile-painting territory battles (suggested 60 s), and Capture, where you close paths to conquer large areas (suggested 120 s)
steal enemy territory and collect power-ups (not described) to reach a domination goal before the timer ends
1-4 players in local multiplayer, with bots of several difficulties filling the slots
territory ranking and end-of-match stats screen
notes: Early web alpha; devlog 0.1.0 'Web alpha is live' dated 1 June 2026, updates through 0.3.0 (5 June 2026). AI-assisted graphics. English and Latin-American Spanish.

title: Chernobyl Girls
mechanics: satirical Soviet theme: claiming area 'cures' mutant pin-up girls
two rounds per patient: reveal the mutant, then the cured version in the same pose; winning both unlocks her poster
Geiger counter: cutting into her silhouette lowers it, time wasted on background raises it; when full, a MELTDOWN ends the attempt
mutant bosses: radioactive aspic, Zmey Gorynych, an armoured train, mutant bears
State Lottery random rewards (vodka, iodine pills, paperwork, 'come back tomorrow')
30 patients, each with a mutation, a job and a story
notes: Published on itch.io 25 Oct 2026, v0.1.1, name-your-own-price. Built on the developer's Waifu's Panic!! engine; that game is a separate $3.99 area-claim game, also on itch.io. The Geiger counter works like a modern take on Gals Panic's monster meter.

title: Chromonia
mechanics: each captured area restores part of a desaturated public-domain painting to full colour
dodge slow, ambient enemies by swapping your colour
no score, timer or punishment (meditative)
public-domain classical music soundtrack
notes: A zen Qix built in Godot 4. Version 1.0.3702 is dated 17 July 2026. The full source is on GitHub (juan-medina/chromonia).

title: Coconut's Coco-Net
mechanics: two-player versus 'sport fighting' built on JezzBall-style walls that claim area
each player can have only one wall active at a time
players can hop over the opponent's wall to take a risk
balls accelerate on each bounce, so each round goes from slow to fast
every button fires a fast grappling hook with momentum, used for movement and attack; the net and ball buttons also carry an item, and holding a button reaches farther to place it
simple defend-only CPU opponent
notes: Fighting Game April Jam 2026 entry (jam ran 31 Mar to 2 May 2026), made in LÖVE 11.5, with a post-jam build in June 2026. The 'All or nothing' wall design and one-wall limit come from the developer's 1 May 2026 devlog. Neither the page nor the devlog says how a round is scored or won.

title: Eight Bit Qix
mechanics: ten-option difficulty menu: lives 1-5, claim goal 50-90% (default 75%), Sparx timer and starting count (2/4/6), Sparx, fuse and Qix speeds, the level where twin Qix appear (1/2/3), extra-life interval (50K/100K/none) and draw speed
presets: Beginner, Arcade (default), Showdown (1 life, no extra lives) and Ruthless (1 life, 85% goal, everything fast)
splitting twin Qix raises the score multiplier up to 9x
notes: An arcade-rules remake built with Love2D. Slow draw scores 300 points per percent and fast draw 150. Stopping mid-line lights a fuse, and the level bonus is 500 points per percent over the goal; these are all base Qix rules. Free. The year is inferred from the itch.io game id (4293270, late 2025 to early 2026).

title: GALS HUNTER
mechanics: destroy enemies by enclosing them in a completed shape or by stomping on them
beating enemies raises the score multiplier
bonus items include a machine gun and a bomb
time bonuses keep the run alive across 10 phases
rank system: the better you play, the more and faster enemies spawn
notes: An itch.io prototype mixing Gals Panic with Every Extend; completing shapes reveals the 'Panic Girl'. It also offers a portable ZIP download and a Spanish-only manual. The page discloses AI-assisted code, graphics and text. The earliest page comments date from 26 Aug 2026.

title: Gravebloom
mechanics: enemy roster with distinct roles: Drifters bounce erratically; Listeners wait until a cut starts, then pursue; Border Wardens patrol the safe edge you must close against; Proximity Mines stay still until approached, then fire
choose one of four vessels, each with one active ability on a single button: DROP dashes through a gap, BELL survives one lethal hit, SEED roots every threat in place, MOTH surges ahead
reclaim 80% to advance; ten hand-authored stages, each hiding a stained-glass window revealed by reclaimed ground
three-layer score per stage
five lives shared across the whole 10-stage run; running out of stage time costs a life
furthest stage is saved; CONTINUE restarts there with five fresh lives
meta collectibles: remembrance pages per vessel and twelve deeds to restore in a churchyard archive
notes: An early build (v0.4.1, Godot 4.7.1) offered free on itch.io, in development. The page places it 'in the tradition of' Qix and Volfied. The itch page discloses AI assistance for code, graphics and sound.

title: Grid Riders
mechanics: GL Tron-inspired car racer; enclose an area with your line to capture it, but only areas connected to your existing territory count (others are discarded)
no trail and slightly higher speed inside your own area
driving through a non-teammate's line destroys that player
cutting a rival's territory off from their start area captures everything disconnected
largest area at the end wins
1-8 players: solo, local split-screen, LAN or server-based online, with teams
notes: Free prototype (v0.7.1), published on itch.io in early November 2026. The page's AI disclosure says Claude wrote much of the code. Capturing by disconnection is a distinctive rule.

title: HIDDEN JOURNEY: ASIA
mechanics: moving without drawing makes the player invincible while an energy gauge lasts; the gauge recovers in that state
drawing (hold Space / A) switches invincibility off; an enemy touching the player or the open line fails the stage
clearing 80% of the mist reveals a photograph of an Asian landscape
notes: Free, AI-assisted code. Devlog 'New title!' dated 13 Feb 2026. Enemy types are not described.

title: Ink Wars
mechanics: score multiplier grows with territory held, so the next capture is worth more
3-minute timed mode against three tactical bots that claim ground and try to cut your trail
score-gated cosmetic unlocks (colours, ball shapes, titles) and a global leaderboard
notes: Free Paper.io-style game in English and Polish; AI-assisted (code, graphics, sounds, text).

title: Lightspace
mechanics: enemy movement synced to the beat of the music
terrain hazards: ice, mirrors, ion storms, fire, teleporters
fire button (Space); the page does not say what it fires
power-ups (unspecified)
five named bosses: the Hunter, the Wraith, the Swarm Queen, the Fortress, the Corrupted Core
7 sectors with 30+ hand-built levels, each sector with its own look and soundtrack; stars per level; Easy/Normal/Hard
a paid Supporter Pack adds a level maker and community levels (play and publish)
notes: Free, published 25 Oct 2026. The Supporter Pack is sold separately. AI-assisted; art, effects and music are generated in code. Keyboard, gamepad and touch.

title: Loop: Land Grab
mechanics: a rival cutting your trail ends the round, so longer excursions grab more but stay exposed longer
bot styles: careful (hug their land), greedy (roam far), aggressive (hunt your trail)
twelve arenas
win at 60% of the field or as the last one standing
separate 90-second timed mode
notes: Published 16 October 2026; free, AI-assisted (code, text); records are saved. The page says the game is available for licensing.

title: Moonlight Territory
mechanics: two line types chosen before leaving the edge: the normal-speed line builds wooden territory, the slow line builds stone forts with double durability
you can retrace the open line to retreat
reaching the stage's occupation target unlocks an auto-aiming bow; dropping to half the target or below seals it again
once the bow is unlocked, wolves chew through walls; a broken wall collapses the territory around it and damages a hunter caught in it
clear condition: kill every wolf, not just reach an area percentage
wolf types: normal; Chaser (signals '!' and pursues a player who is drawing); Dasher (charges, then dashes with sudden turns); new wolves appear over time
2-player co-op with shared territory and shared life, occupation tracked per player
5 stages with targets rising to 80%
notes: Free, published 31 Oct 2026, AI-assisted. The page recommends a PC keyboard.

title: NEON CUT
mechanics: colour-matching objective: capture the bouncing shapes of the target colour for points
wrong-coloured shapes must be kept from reaching your open line
bouncing shapes get in the way of cuts
three lives, no time limit
notes: Free, published 2 Nov 2026, AI-assisted. Scoring values and how lives are lost are not described.

title: Neon Divide
mechanics: each cell of the open circuit adds value; cutting deeper toward the central Core raises the score multiplier (more risk, more reward)
six hostile types, each with a distinct behaviour tell and a shape marker (not colour-only)
five bosses with distinct fights
15 run upgrades: pick one of three after each Arcade Run clear (roguelite)
