a hostile spider interferes, and the player races it to uncover the picture
notes: A Ukrainian-language children's edutainment game from the 'Дитяча колекція' series that covers painting history from cave art to Ukrainian artists. Old-Games.ru calls 'Моя територія' 'an analogue of Qix/Xonix' with a picture opened 'in a race against an evil spider'. Other mini-games in the title include a Tetris variant that reveals a picture.

title: Boku no Natsuyasumi 4 (QIX 50-yen game)
alt_titles: ぼくのなつやすみ4 瀬戸内少年探偵団「ボクと秘密の地図」
mechanics: Taito's QIX is playable inside a summer-vacation life sim as the '50-yen game' at the Yoshida shop, paid with in-game pocket money
notes: Released 2 July 2009, with a 'PSP the Best' budget re-release on 7 July 2011. Japanese Wikipedia (both the game and the Qix article) says Taito's QIX can be played as the 50-yen game at 吉田商店. A 2013 Dengeki review lists 'ミニゲーム『QIX』' among the game's additions. The sources do not document the minigame's rules.
sources: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ぼくのなつやすみ4_瀬戸内少年探偵団「ボクと秘密の地図」

title: Clubhouse Games: 51 Worldwide Classics (Dots and Boxes)
mechanics: turn-based: draw one line between two adjacent dots per turn
completing the fourth side of a box claims it and grants another turn
most boxes claimed wins
notes: Dots and Boxes is game #2 of 51; Hex (#7) is also included. Released 5 June 2020. Additional work credited to CAProduction.

title: KISS U
mechanics: fantasy dating-sim visual novel with fast mini-games; VNDB tags one as a Xonix/Qix-style capture game, in which boxed-off areas reveal a hidden picture
the capture mini-game's specific rules are not documented
notes: Demos released 2022-03-29 and 2025-06-24 (VNDB). Wikidata lists Gals Panic as an inspiration. Adult-rated (nudity); charming characters unlocks pinup photos. Full game crowdfunded via Kickstarter and planned for Steam (PC/Mac).

title: Coin-Op Vice
mechanics: Xonix is one of 100+ short altered arcade mini-games played on machines inside a 2.5D top-down action game
completing an arcade rewards two random cartridges (skills, weapons, abilities), which make up a deck; two cartridges combine into a higher-level one, and deck size grows with the detective's rank
arcade buildings and rooms are procedurally generated, with 8 main missions and daily random missions
notes: Released September 26, 2024. The Steam page names Xonix among the mini-games but does not describe its territory rules.

title: Erix
platforms: Ericsson mobile phones (seen on the T39m)
notes: A May 2008 revision of Wikipedia's Qix article says: 'Erix is a Qix clone, which has been seen in the software for at least one Ericsson phone model (the T39m) around 2000-2001.' The T39 shipped in 2001. No gameplay details found.

title: JezzBall (Softex, J2ME)
notes: Version 1.0.0 appears twice in the libretro/No-Intro J2ME dat (CRC A46997A4 and CD5FB7EC; jars of about 9.6 KB). Gameplay is undocumented. It is presumed to be a JezzBall clone from its title.

title: Nyamida Monogatari
notes: Straight clone: a mobile version of Amidar with cats and mice in place of the original characters, cited in Japanese Wikipedia to a 2002 GAME Watch report. The article names neither the publisher nor the handset platform.

title: Megami Tensei QIX Persona 3
alt_titles: 女神転生QIX ペルソナ3
developer: unknown (not named; copyright credits ATLUS and TAITO)
publisher: Atlus and BBMF (via the 'Megaten α' mobile site)
mechanics: Enemies are Persona 3 Shadows drawn as their masks.
Clearing a stage takes 80% instead of 75%.
Each stage has 3 lives. Touching an enemy, or your own line while drawing outside your territory, costs one.
The player is invincible while inside their own claimed territory.
Enclosing an area defeats the enemies inside it, but the large white-masked boss Shadow cannot be killed by enclosure.
Pickups are collected by enclosing them: a red card gives a temporary speed-up, a blue card temporarily slows enemies, and a yellow card gives an extra life.
Enclosed areas reveal official Persona 3 illustrations by Shigenori Soejima, set to Persona 3 BGM.
Clearing a stage unlocks a phone wallpaper, and replaying a cleared stage at 86% or more unlocks another.
notes: A licensed Japanese feature-phone tie-in made under Taito's Qix licence. It cost 315 yen per download. It launched alongside the puzzle app 'Megami Tensei CHAINING SOUL PERSONA3'.

title: Bix
mechanics: Swiping anywhere on the screen steers the tracer in that direction, and a double-tap pauses.
Closing a line fills the side with fewer balls, a JezzBall-style rule replacing Qix's 'side without the Qix'.
2008 ball types: normal, bouncing, respawning (survives being enclosed), slow-down (pauses, then slows all balls) and 1-up. Trapping a special ball triggers its power.
Fill 75% to clear, with 3 lives.
Bix Challenge (2015 onward) has 100 levels in 10 galaxies, each with its own twist: ball traps, line limits, dark zones, time trials, giant balls, ice walls or hunters.
The Rift: a hidden endless climb after level 100.
Up to three stars per level, plus chests, gold balls and coins.
Boosters: Slow Start and Shield.
Weekly Race: one shared board a week, raced to 75% for medals.
A continue option for stuck players, and a 'Classic version' toggle that restores the 2008 game.
notes: Two Padadaz listings both launched on 31 Oct 2008: 'Bix' (id294842200, last updated 2017) and 'Bix Challenge' (id294848792, rebuilt in 2015 and updated again in 2020-21 and 2025). The modern galaxy campaign is in Bix Challenge. AppBank reviewed the original at 115 yen, with a free version. The research agent's claim that it reached top-5 charts in France, Germany and the UK isn't supported by any fetched source, so I removed it.

title: BurnBall
notes: Listed as 'BurnBall - iPhone game with same gameplay' in the external links of Wikipedia's JezzBall article from 15 Dec 2008, so it was released by then (first iPhone App Store year). The Gamicus wiki keeps the same link, and the Qixote list has it under 'Sundry'. Gameplay is not documented beyond being the same as JezzBall.

title: Eyestorm
publisher: Vivid Apps (App Store seller: Jens Egeblad)
mechanics: swipe across the screen to build walls of blocks
several eye enemy types: some bounce like JezzBall balls, some move randomly or in patterns, some spawn more eyes
UFO enemies
boss fights
puzzle levels
power-ups
story campaign against Dr. Eyequeue
easy, normal and hard difficulty (added in a January 2010 update)
28 levels plus a secret level (the Lite version has 12)
notes: Lite version 1.0 was released April 10, 2009. Only the Lite version is still listed. The listing says it adds 'power-ups, bosses, and puzzles' to 'Jezzball, Styx, and Xonix like games' and cites 5 enemy types.

title: Jezz
mechanics: claim 70% of the field per level (JezzBall asks for 75%)
each level adds more balls
notes: Released March 21, 2009 for iPhone and iPod touch. It was Menial's first iPhone game, with graphics by Kevin Andersson (IconDesign). It is a close JezzBall remake: a ball hitting an unfinished wall destroys it and costs a life. An App Store search no longer shows it.

title: Spider: The Secret of Bryce Manor
alt_titles: Spider: The Secret of Bryce Manor Director's Cut
mechanics: the spider trails silk when it jumps between surfaces, and a strand breaks if the gap is too wide
closing a triangle of strands forms a web that catches the insects inside it
a per-level insect quota opens the exit portal, and play may continue after it
hornets (added in the Director's Cut) cannot be webbed and must be killed by jumping into them
modes: Adventure, Feeding Frenzy (time limit), Hunger (endless), Precision (limited silk)
notes: Adjacent genre: a side-view take on enclosing shapes to capture moving targets, and Precision mode makes the trail a limited resource. Prequel to Spider: Rite of the Shrouded Moon, which the Qixote wiki lists under 'Closish Enough'.

title: Trap!
notes: Linked as 'Trap!, a JezzBall clone for the Android OS' (androidfreeware.net) in Wikipedia's JezzBall article from 20 Aug 2009, so it was released by then. Gameplay is not documented beyond being a JezzBall clone.

title: iSlash
mechanics: swipe across the shape to cut it at any angle; the cut is instant, with no marker walking the edge
the cut-off part without ninja stars is removed; each level asks you to trim away most of the shape, and the amount grows over time
bouncing ninja stars at different speeds, near-invisible ghost stars, and later bamboo stars, comet stars and mother stars that release babies
a saw enemy that kills on touch but can itself be slashed
metal edges that cannot be cut (a paid Power Blade lets you cut them)
trap the stars in as few cuts as possible
paid power-up packs: Skip Master, Star Killer, Time Bender, Power Blade
real-time multiplayer: simultaneous slashing races on 50 multiplayer levels (added in a later version)
240 levels in the current listing (70 at launch, per an October 2010 review)
notes: Released August 26, 2010 on iOS. Wikipedia lists it among Qix clones as 'iSlash (2010, iOS, Duello)'. Its bouncing-star, instant-cut rules sit closer to JezzBall. The spinoffs named earlier (iSlash Heroes, iSlash DOJO) were not verified.

title: XonixAttack
developer: unknown (package com.oidapps.xonixattack; announced by forum user mandrazhoid)
notes: Straight clone: you move a green xonix to cut the field, claim 75% and avoid red and white enemy xonixes, with touch, trackball or D-pad control. The announcement says it is inspired by Qix, Xonix and JezzBall. It is no longer on Google Play.

title: Curvebot Evolved
mechanics: A robot runs along the edges of 3D planes. Pressing both touch buttons sends it straight across, drawing an edge-to-edge cut.
Each cut removes the part on one side. The aim is to shrink the plane to a target fraction (about 20%) instead of claiming 75%.
Enemies learn to spot your cut lines and try to cut across them.
Energy-zapping robots and other obstacles.
Later planes have awkward shapes.
72 levels.
notes: 148Apps reviewed it on 7 Oct 2011 (by Sinan Kubba) and lists iOS, Android and Windows Phone. The developer name 'Elpixo' comes from the research agent's search snippet and is not confirmed by any fetched page.

title: JezzBall Classic
mechanics: 83 rule mods usable alone or combined, some changing play (for example two wallbuilders at once), with separate high scores per combination
22 preset mod combinations
100 puzzle rooms solved by well-timed wall placement
missions that challenge personal bests
optional real photos (700) placed into the built walls each level, so captured area reveals a picture
notes: A faithful recreation of 1992 JezzBall's graphics, sound, scoring, physics and tempo at a higher frame rate. A level ends when over 75% is built, and each level adds one atom. iOS release September 12, 2011 at $4.99; the free Lite followed September 23, 2011. A PC version was announced on itch.io on April 16, 2016, alongside Android and iOS 2.0.0 versions.

title: Tarantula vs Snake
mechanics: A spider claims area by spinning a web, and each level needs a 'sufficiently large' web instead of a fixed percentage.
A hungry snake hunts the spider instead of Qix and Sparks.
Endless levels of rising difficulty, with a global leaderboard.
Two-player co-op on one device, working together against the snake.
Tilt control in early versions (1.1-1.2.1), and later gamepad support (PlayStation, Xbox, MFi).
notes: Version 1.0 came out on 7 Dec 2011. The description cites Qix, JezzBall, Styx and Xonix as inspirations, but doesn't explain exactly how the web claims area.

title: Sweet Split
mechanics: walls can be drawn at any angle by dragging, not only horizontally or vertically
each level adds one more bouncing sweet; a wrong line costs a life
fill 75% of the free space
4 power-up items to grab at the right moment (Arcade mode)
unlockable Zen mode with infinite lives and no rules
Level Mode: 140+ handmade levels in packs with 3-star ratings; Arcade mode has an online global high-score list
notes: Version 1.0 came out December 29/30, 2012. The features are from the current listing (still updated in 2026), so some may postdate the first release.

title: Xonix Blast
mechanics: blue balls leave mines behind them
red balls split chunks off already-filled territory and turn them back into dangerous area
missiles (double tap) calm enemies
teleport (long press) jumps through the enemy area to a safe region, collecting bonuses on the way
bonuses that slow or stop enemies or speed up the player
extra points for fast clears and overfills buy bonuses or an assistant bot in an 'Ammunition' shop
a purchasable assistant bot plays alongside you and fills part of the field
reversing into the dangerous area is not allowed (flick controls)
filled areas show colourful landscape images
32 levels free, 96 in the full version
notes: Announced on Android Central on 29 Mar 2012 by OmegaLabs, with Play packages com.omegalabs.xonixblastfree and com.omegalabs.xonixblast, both now delisted. The post says it is 'mostly similar to the father's version for PC' with features added for Android. Red balls that re-open claimed land are unusual for the genre. The developer said a later version would add timed countdown levels.

title: Dig!
mechanics: Digging replaces line drawing: an archaeologist digs lines through his backyard and must dig out 75% of each level.
Nigel the mummy roams the level, and if he touches your dig line, more enemies are unleashed (for example, moles with fezzes).
Artifacts dug up earn money for power-ups and perk-giving hats.
Exhibit pieces fill museum collections, which pay the hero a salary (a meta-progression loop).
Levels go deeper and deeper toward the centre of the earth.
notes: The App Store description says it is 'Inspired by the arcade game "QiX"'. It runs on iPhone and iPad. Version 1.0 is dated 25 Apr 2013, and the store's release date is 9 May 2013. The seller is Crescent Moon Games LLC, which mostly publishes, so the actual developer may be a separate studio.

title: Kids Xonix
developer: unknown (package kidsxonix.game.sp; announced by forum user tihan)
mechanics: the claimed area is themed as a girl (Lily) sowing seeds that turn bare ground into grass and flowers
bug enemies
24 levels; clears earn 12 collectible animal rewards
notes: A Xonix variant for children, announced on Android Central on 4 Oct 2013. The Play listing (kidsxonix.game.sp) is now delisted.

title: The Filling
mechanics: touching your own line costs a life
Episodes mode: 80 levels in 5 episodes with several enemy kinds
on some Episodes levels the perimeter is not a safe zone
Arcade mode: the enemy count keeps rising, with three difficulty levels
swipe-anywhere gesture steering that can chain direction changes
notes: Version 1.0 released 13 Feb 2013 for $0.99 and updated through v2.9.3 (Nov 2023). The developer cites Qix and Gals Panic, and the Intro also cites Xonix. A free 12-level demo, 'The Filling Intro', followed on 26 Jan 2015.

title: Line Knight Fortix
mechanics: Enclosing an enemy's position cuts it out of the map and captures it: dragons, ogres and turrets.
Larger enclosures capture several targets at once for more points, but take longer and carry more risk.
Blood bats and bone dragons seek out the player and disrupt drawing.
Fire-breathing dragons and turrets that fire projectiles.
Collected keys unlock new areas of a stage.
Power-ups, and unlockable weapons such as catapults that remove enemies permanently.
Steered by dragging anywhere on screen, with a zoomable camera.
45 levels.
notes: An iOS re-imagining of Nemesys Games' Fortix PC games, with a medieval theme. It cost $0.99 and was reviewed in January 2014 (148Apps on 13 Jan, Cult of Mac on 17 Jan).

title: Qix Galaxy: Space Adventure
mechanics: Dragging a finger steers a spaceship, which replaces the Qix cursor.
Each stage is cleared by fencing off a set percentage of the screen around a planet.
Coins earned in play buy gradual ship upgrades.
Obstacles, plus homing missiles that chase the ship if it doesn't keep moving, which punishes stalling.
Freemium structure: a lives system, ads after each level, and a separate currency for continues.
notes: 148Apps reviewed it on 29 Apr 2014 (3.5/5, by Jennifer Allen) and criticised the freemium elements. It has no Game Center support, so scores are shared through Facebook only. The game has been pulled from the App Store: the store pages and iTunes lookup return nothing. The research agent's further claims (60 levels with missions, stars for capturing most of the screen and killing all enemies, the Qix appearing only as a boss, a Captain Gordon story, Unity, an Android version, a Taito licence) came from pages that now return 403 or 404. They could not be checked and are left out of mechanics.

title: Split: Ball Trap Arcade
mechanics: swipe vertically or horizontally to start a partition wall that expands toward both edges
a ball hitting the wall before it reaches both edges destroys it
reach the target percentage to clear the level
notes: The Google Play listing (com.split.android) was first published 8 Aug 2014 and has 100K+ installs and about 2.2K ratings. The current description bills it as a modern JezzBall revival, and the last update was 29 Jul 2026. The listing does not say whether the 2014 release carried the same developer name. Contains ads and in-app purchases.

title: 国盗り Returns with 閃乱カグラ NewWave
mechanics: a virtual pad replaces swipe controls so a finger does not cover the art
single-player, a harder Hell Mode, and PvP against friends' replay data
each stage's score unlocks up to four illustration cards; the 3rd and 4th are 18+ images in a separate code-gated "Diary" viewer
free-to-play with an omikuji-style gacha whose cost doubles each pull and that guarantees every item within 12 pulls
notes: A Korean, Senran Kagura-licensed line-drawing game. Android launched in South Korea on 19 November 2014, and iOS was planned for January 2015. It draws on about 1,500 illustrations, 600 of them in the game. The service has ended.

title: Cool Xonix
notes: Ukrainian Wikipedia links an archived dojoy.ru/ru/mobile/coolxonix page (snapshot 16 Feb 2015) as a 'Xonix sequel for iOS and Android'. dojoy.ru is now a board-game publisher and the page returns 404. The app is not in the current App Store or Play catalogues. AlternativeTo, the only source for Windows support and for 'bonuses collected on the field make levels easier', was blocked (403), so both claims are unverified.

title: Pix Panic
year: 2015 or earlier (Google Play version updated 8 December 2015)
mechanics: capture lines are drawn at any angle ("360 degrees of freedom"): tap and drag outside the border to set waypoints for the capture path
tap inside the revealed border to move along its edge while sparks patrol it
a boss fires lasers, and the boss or its lasers hitting the line in progress loses it
reveal 80% of the silhouetted image to clear
notes: The Google Play listing calls it "a Qix style game in the vein of the Gals Panic S series". The itch.io page calls it "a qix-like game with 360 degrees of freedom" and offers name-your-price Windows .exe and .jar builds. Their itch.io game id suggests they were added after the Android release.

title: Spider Web: Akai's Journey
mechanics: swipe to move and weave a thread; returning to the edge closes an area, and the smaller part is revealed
uncover the whole postcard to finish a level; 80 levels in 4 worlds each unlock a postcard and an animated scene
enemies catch you by touching the thread; new enemy types in almost every level, up to giant bosses
up to three stars per level (240 in total)
notes: Released on the App Store on 17 October 2015 (Apple lookup data). Version 2.0.1 followed in October 2026.

title: Xonix Assault
mechanics: soldier theme: the enemies are artillery that you destroy by trapping them
clear 80% within a per-level time limit; running out of time costs a life
notes: Google Play shows a release date of 30 Aug 2015 and a last update of 23 Mar 2016.

title: Zombie Brain Seizure
mechanics: slice the field with lines; if a bouncing brain touches a line before it is finished, you lose
bigger slices score more, rewarding risk over safe small cuts
claim 75% to clear a level; 50 levels with new brain patterns and behaviours
power-ups: slow time, make brains vanish briefly, skip a level
3-star rating per level, with replays to improve
notes: Version 1.0 came out June 24, 2015. The listing calls it Qix-style, but the bouncing brains and slicing lines are JezzBall-like. The features are from the current listing.

title: Animal Volfied
mechanics: shrinking the open area traps and destroys enemies
bonuses speed up the player or stop enemies
claim more than 80% to pass a level
notes: Turkish animal-themed Volfied clone. iOS 1.0 was released 3 Oct 2016. The Google Play listing is dated Feb-Mar 2026 and has few installs, so the Android version may be a recent release.

title: Pakal
mechanics: planets split into areas, each with three gold-leaf objectives: reach the minimum capture percentage, destroy all enemies, destroy all bases and obstructions
gold leaves unlock later planets
each round has a time limit
completing an area shows a photo of the uncovered territory
5 lives, refilled by watching ads or made unlimited by a purchase
notes: The store page says it is inspired by Volfied and Qix; the player is the astronaut Pacal. Released 20 Sep 2016, last updated May 2021. Themed planets added later include Candy, Car, Bike, Monster and Bikini, and the app is rated 13+ for suggestive content.

title: Stealin
mechanics: the player steers a tank around the field (swipe and hold) and divides the field with horizontal or vertical lines (swipe)
enemy soldiers bouncing off the walls cannot touch the tank while it is capturing
capture a supermajority of the field
15+ enemy types plus land obstacles
36 story levels, each with several possible solutions
notes: Released March 5, 2016. The developer bills it as 'like old good Qix but with tanks!' The story follows a tank retaking Whiteslope from the dictator Stealin, with tank-history facts between levels. It went free with ads in August 2020.

title: Volfield
developer: Umut Isik (Play Store name: Penguen Umut)
mechanics: bonus boxes: +1000 points, extra shield time, freeze enemies, destroy all small enemies, extra ship
penalty boxes: -1000 points, reduced shield time, lose a ship, which makes opening boxes a gamble
the player can set a custom background image for each level
Arcade Mode plus a 36-level Level Mode; claim at least 80% to pass
different enemies in each level
leaderboards for 24 hours, 7 days and all time, plus by country
notes: Self-described homage to Volfied, Qix and Gals Panic. Free with ads; last updated 2022 (version 3.1).

title: Code: Xonix
mechanics: clear 80% of the dark area within a time limit
several enemy types
Level mode with 25 stages of rising difficulty
Random mode that builds games from the enemy types met in Level mode
notes: Version 1.0 released 5 Sep 2017 and updated to 1.04 (May 2018). It is free, with a $0.99 remove-ads purchase. The store describes it as taking 'a very old game running on Windows 95' and adding many improvements.

title: Mr Super Fish: Hero Fill Block
publisher: Classic Arcade Games (copyright holder on the App Store listing)
mechanics: four enemy classes, each tied to a terrain: Ms Jelly Fish roams only open space, Pac Crab roams only filled (captured) blocks, Sea Snails Xon travel along the walls, Ball Fish Man roams open space and eats wall blocks (un-fills captured ground)
item drops: Blue Fish freezes enemies, Green Leaf slows enemies, a pink item lets the player eat enemies, a Pill speeds the player up
a level clears at more than 80% filled
50-level mode plus an endless mode
swipe controls in four directions
notes: Each enemy class is defined by which terrain it moves on. The listing shows a 2016 copyright by Classic Arcade Games, but the earliest version in its history is 1.1 (28 Oct 2017), and v1.3 (31 Oct 2017) added 30 levels for 50 in total. v1.4 removed enemy speed acceleration.

title: String.io
mechanics: map made of hexagon blocks; enclose an area with your string to capture it
hitting another player's tail eliminates them
up to 4 selectable control modes
notes: 10M+ installs; last updated 4 Aug 2026. Online PvP is still listed as 'coming soon', so play is against AI. Package id io.hexargame.stringpaperio.

title: ChetBall
mechanics: draw lines to close off regions of the canvas around bouncing balls
close 75% of the canvas to advance
each level adds more balls and more speed
notes: A straight JezzBall clone, released February 21, 2018; the last update was May 2018. Free with a $2.99 no-ads purchase.

title: Qiks!
developer: unknown (Voodoo is the seller; the listing's copyright line credits Pangolapp / App Advisory)
mechanics: the field is a board of blocks; swipe to send the player across and fill blocks, revealing a hidden pixel-art image
touching an enemy ends the attempt
limited lives that refill over time (per user reviews)
notes: A hyper-casual Qix released on 17 May 2019 by Voodoo, the Paper.io publisher. The block grid makes it close to Xonix, but the goal is an image reveal.

title: Split Area - Brain Arcade game
mechanics: draw a slicer line that cuts the board; a ball touching the line before the cut completes costs a life
score by trapping the balls in the smallest possible areas
stars to collect on the board
Endless mode with worldwide leaderboards, plus a level map where more balls appear as levels get harder
notes: Version 1.0 released 13 Aug 2019; last update 2 Jul 2023 (v1.3.19).

title: SPLITRON
mechanics: drag a finger to draw a line; it becomes a border only when the finger is lifted
black tiles in an enclosed ball-free area shatter to reveal a landscape picture
each landscape spans five stages, each adding balls and difficulty
notes: iOS version 1.0 came out April 5/6, 2019; free with ads and still updated in 2026. A Google Play listing titled 'Splitron' exists (package com.kaeguree.inclose), but its details did not render.

title: Xonix Worlds Iceland
mechanics: theme swap: a penguin reclaims melted parts of Iceland, and sharks and orcas are the enemies
one-touch controls
levels get progressively harder
notes: v1.0 dated 7 May 2019, last update v1.1.0 on 25 Jan 2020. The store page gives only a short description.

title: Air Xonix: Remastered
publisher: Andrii Serba (current Google Play developer account)
mechanics: 3D remake of the look and music of the 2001 PC game Air Xonix: a craft cuts off sections of a 3D board
main episodes plus Challenge levels and Daily Events, with different layouts and enemy combinations
bouncing enemies and hazards
PvP mode and unlockable skins (Nov 2026 update notes)
notes: Package com.DelicoGames.Xonix, released on Google Play on 14 Dec 2020, with 100,000+ installs. It was listed earlier as 'Xonix 3D - Classic Arcade Game' (BlueStacks, credited to Delico Games). The listing calls it 'inspired by' the 2001 PC Air Xonix, so it is a homage, not the original; the claim from a Wikipedia mirror that Delico made AirXonix is unsupported. I found no source for the alt title 'Air Xonix Qix Arcade Game'.

title: Air Xonix: Remastered
developer: Delico Games (Google Play account: Andrii Serba)
mechanics: Challenge levels and Daily Events on top of the main episodes, with different layouts and enemy combinations
hazards in addition to bouncing enemies
PvP mode (per the update notes)
unlockable skins (per the update notes)
touch controls designed for short mobile sessions
notes: The package com.DelicoGames.Xonix first went on Google Play on 14 Dec 2020. The same account also publishes other com.DelicoGames apps, such as Crowd Rush Zombie Riot. This listing may therefore be the Delico Games Android 'Xonix 3D' recorded elsewhere in the catalog, now under a new name; check for a duplicate. Its 3D graphics and music are modelled on the 2001 PC game AirXonix. The description says 'inspired by' AirXonix, so this is not presented as a licensed remaster. Contains ads and in-app purchases; 100K+ downloads.

title: Area of Pirates
mechanics: You set a sailing route by touch, and completing a voyage charts that sea area. The goal is to complete the whole map.
Pirates must not notice you: their sight is the threat, not only contact.
Pirates carry a variety of weapons.
notes: Version 1.0 came out on 19 Feb 2020. It is free and supports English and Korean. Its mission line reads 'complete the map without being noticed by pirates'. The store description is truncated, so the exact enclosure rule is unconfirmed. It is from the same studio as Sneak Peeling.

title: FillBottom
mechanics: drag to draw a line marking where a row of blocks will be built; releasing starts building it
a guarding ball ends the game if it detects the line while it is being built
once the line completes, blocks pile up to fill it, filling the floor; a ball they hit bursts
keep filling the floor as blocks collapse, playing for distance
notes: Released on Google Play 19 Oct 2020 and on iOS 23 Oct 2020; Android updated 11 Aug 2025 (100+ installs). Same developer as SPLITRON and Sneak Peeling.

title: Jezz (Max Lund)
mechanics: drag and hold to place a horizontal or vertical wall
the wall starts building only when the finger is released
a ball hitting the wall while it builds destroys it
notes: Released on Google Play 17 Jul 2020; last updated 23 Mar 2023 (v1.1.3); 5K+ installs. Distinct from the 2009 iOS 'Jezz' by Menial in the catalogue.

title: Paper.io 3D
mechanics: territory is drawn over the surfaces of 3D shapes instead of a flat board
stars to collect during play
level-based: reach 100% coverage to clear a level and unlock new levels and bonuses
notes: Level-based 3D spin-off of Paper.io; 50M+ installs. Last updated 8 Sep 2026.

title: Sneak Peeling
mechanics: You draw a freehand closed shape anywhere instead of tracing from the border. On release, the board is cut along it over time.
A fire demon guards the board, and if it detects the cut in progress, the attempt fails. Stealth replaces line collision.
The fire demon interferes in several other ways.
An undetected cut peels away the black board to reveal part of the background image, and the stage is cleared by occupying all of it.

100 levels across 10 worlds
leaderboard ranks cumulative score across all levels (v1.0.1)
notes: v1.0 released on 10 Mar 2026. Short store description, so the mechanics are only coarsely documented.

title: Starcutter: Space Arcade
mechanics: an enemy touching the line while it is drawn starts a fuse racing toward the player
closing a line claims the area the boss cannot reach; each cut reveals more of a painted world

10 bosses, each with one trick: dashing, hunting the line, hatching drones, sowing mines, teleporting, shockwaves, eating claimed land, sweeping a light beam, a dangerous reflection; the final boss (Void Crown) uses all of them
'Cage the Boss' large bonus for finishing a sector at 90% or 95%
crates: boost, freeze, laser, purge, extra time, Nova (destroys the boss outright)
daily challenge: the same three sectors for everyone, with a shared leaderboard
Expedition: three sectors in a row with an upgrade chosen between them
relaxed mode without the clock
versus: two players on one iPad or with controllers, or online quick match and private rooms
10 worlds, 40 sectors, 120 stars
notes: Released 6 Nov 2026. Free tier (worlds 1-2, daily challenge, one versus duel per session) with a $2.99 full unlock; no ads.

title: TerraFill: Territory Capture
mechanics: touching your own unfinished line costs a life
spider enemies learn new tricks as levels climb
hand-built levels with rising target percentages
'leaves' currency buys an extra life, a shield or a freeze
Mystery Crates every 6 hours give leaves, spare lives, head starts or skins (Oct 2026 update)
daily missions and streaks
notes: Explicitly modelled on Qix and Xonix; plays offline. Released on 22 Aug 2026 (listed as 21 Aug in the US store data) and updated on 29 Oct 2026; 1,000+ downloads.

title: Territory Arcade
mechanics: a line can start anywhere on the edge of your territory
a closed cut keeps the enemy-free side: with enemies on both sides you keep the smaller half, and on a clear field the larger half
a speed cap on the cutter makes long cuts risky
three bouncing enemy types with steady, readable paces: Dasher (smallest, fastest), Reflector (baseline), Heavy (nearly twice the size at a little over half the speed)
Slow Time and Shield pickups on the board trigger on touch
100 hand-crafted stages in themed acts, with per-stage targets rising from 60% to 90%
each stage earns 1-3 stars from completion percentage, time and lives remaining
notes: iOS v1.0 came out on 27 May 2026 and Android on 9 Sep 2026. iOS v1.0.8 notes say the store text now 'matches the game exactly'. No ads, no purchases. Site: ootssu.com.

title: Territory Run: Arcade Capture
mechanics: a 'SCAN' percentage: each captured area reveals more of a hidden image
Bonus Levels with different backgrounds and visual challenges
multiple worlds of progressively harder levels, with stars and lives
Core Reward crates that grant power-ups: Shield, Freeze, Speed Boost and Enemy Elimination
enemies with different movement patterns; an enemy touching the active trail costs a life
swipe controls
notes: The listing cites Qix and Volfied as inspirations. Released on Google Play 29 May 2026, updated 27 Sep 2026. Plays offline.

title: Territory: Claim & Conquer
mechanics: once off safe land the trail cannot be stopped; releasing the thumb does not save you
closing a loop claims every pocket the enemies can no longer reach, and enemies sealed inside are destroyed

six enemy types: Drifter (occupies space), Hunter (commits to your trail and accelerates), Orbiter (arcs wide), Chaos (no fixed direction), Shadow (fades out and moves fastest while invisible), Sentinel (walks the edge of your own land, so the border is never safe)
score scales with the area taken in one loop, how long the line was exposed and the number of loops closed without dying; one long pass is worth about six times a small claim

modes: Classic (three lives, levels introduce new behaviour rather than bigger numbers), Endless (one ever-tightening board), Time Attack (beat the clock with one life), Zen (no enemies, no failure, no timer)
Daily Challenge: the same board for every player each day
notes: Scores exposure time as risk. The shared daily board and the long-pass multiplier bear directly on seeded runs. No version history is shown on the listing (single release, late 2026). Requires iOS 16.4; no ads or purchases.

title: Volfi: Cyber Territory Arcade
mechanics: non-rectangular arenas: Octagon, Diamond, Cross, Star, Citadel
the clear target varies from 75% to 85% per arena; reaching it destroys the guardian boss
minions trapped inside a cut give large bonus points
named bosses (Crimson Crab, Laser Viper, Iron Scarab, Plasma Mantis, Arachno Core, Quantum Eye) across 20+ galaxy episodes and 200+ stages
4 power-ups: Cryo Freeze, Overdrive Speed, Aegis Shield, EMP Crush Wave
permanent hangar upgrades: thrusters, shield reactor, trail insulator, score multiplier
30-tier season pass and 48-hour star tournaments with a win-streak score multiplier up to 10x
notes: The store page says it is inspired by Volfied and Qix. The Google Play listing (com.attara.volfi) is dated 3-4 Nov 2026 and shows 0+ installs.

title: VolfieD (3Dmobiles)
notes: Package com.volfied.volfied; contains ads; rated Everyone; 500+ downloads. The store text only promises 'classic Volfied-style' territory capture with stages that get harder, so it lists nothing that differs from base Qix/Volfied. No release date is shown on the listing.

title: Voltcore
mechanics: 7 enemy types: Wanderers, Trackers, Edge Hunters, Splitters, Spikes, Stalkers, Bosses
12 map patterns, including walls, fortresses, spirals and scattered obstacles
100 levels across 6 difficulty tiers; up to 3 stars per level
boss battles at levels 30, 50, 70, 80, 90, 95 and 100
enemies can be crushed by trapping them in corners (added in 1.0.1)
Shield and Timewarp power-ups
notes: Inspired by Qix and Volfied-style games. Released 20 May 2026. The store claims no ads, but the privacy label lists advertising data.

title: VOLTFIELD: 80s Classic Arcade
mechanics: the ship never stops; swipe to turn
claiming enough opens an exit gate; the player may leave or keep carving for more stars
enemies hunt the live wire and grow more aggressive the deeper you cut; one touch ends the run
hazards: burning walls, moving fire bars, rotors, arc gates and currents that push the ship
10 boss fights against the Wardens, each in its own arena
boosters: homing bolt, pulse bomb, mines, ghost wire, breaker, overdrive
Daily Volt: one new field per day, identical for every player, 3 attempts, with shared leaderboards
100 handmade levels across 10 sectors
notes: Made 'in the spirit of' Qix and Volfied. Released 8 Aug 2026. The shared daily field is relevant to seeded competitive play.

title: World Tour Qix
mechanics: each level starts as a black-and-white landmark postcard that captured territory reveals in colour
levels are world cities reached by flying an airplane across an illustrated world map
four seasons (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter), each with its own colours, visual effects and gameplay variations
pink spiders crawl along the borders and electric spheres bounce across the open field
unlocked postcards carry historical facts, and each capital adds a passport stamp
online leaderboard for runs played without continues, plus a daily leaderboard (v1.2)
notes: Released on Google Play on 22 Jul 2026 as 'Qix - World Tour' and on the App Store on 6 Aug 2026 (v1.0) as 'World Tour Qix'. Italian developer (ffz.it).

title: XonixMinimal
mechanics: themed around cats and bricks, with several cats starting from different sides of the screen
10 curated realms with a hint shown before each
Inverse Mode: eliminated cats respawn after a 3-second delay
seasonal Easter Bunny mode with bunny-styled bricks
notes: The v1.7 notes announce a rebrand to 'Cats vs. Bricks', but the store title is still XonixMinimal. The earliest listed version is v1.4 (30 Jan 2026), with a 2026 copyright; the app requires iOS 26.1, so v1.0 may date from late 2025. The listing has no feature description and never states the capture rules, so the Xonix lineage rests on the title.

title: YiNe - Territory Capture
mechanics: draw lines edge to edge to secure zones
trap the main enemy while avoiding moving obstacles
claim at least 80% of the map
grid maps with per-level visual themes and custom enemies
bonus stages: navigate dark paths to collect useful items
medals for higher stages
notes: Google Play shows 7 Oct 2026 as both the release and the update date; 50+ downloads.

title: Zoooo: Classic Area Capture
mechanics: captures restore a grey illustration to colour
rescue the animal hidden in each picture by restoring the area around it; its card goes into a collectible album
items: Speed Boost, Shield, Enemy Freeze
no time pressure; each mission sets a target area to restore
swipe controls
notes: A cozy picture-reveal Qix with collectibles, made in Godot; the itch.io page discloses AI-assisted code and text. Released on Google Play 18 Aug 2026, updated 25 Sep 2026. The itch.io page only links to the Google Play listing.

title: 땅따먹기 (GLORIOGO)
mechanics: clear at a target share of 75% or more
50 stages, each revealing a themed photo shoot (racing models, K-pop idols, pilots, baristas, orchestra conductors); cleared photos go to a gallery
booster items: Freeze, Shield, Speed
bosses and minions get faster as stages progress
choice of virtual D-pad or touch-drag controls
notes: Version 1.0.0, released 29 Oct 2026 on Google Play (package com.ttalkkag.ddangda). The English store page keeps the Korean title; its description calls the game 'Territory Capture'. Contains ads.

title: 땅따먹기왕 : 꼬리로 둘러싸는 땅따먹기
mechanics: character slides across a slightly tilted board following the finger
leaving your land grows a tail; returning claims the enclosed area, including opponents' land
stepping on a robot's tail destroys it; stepping on your own tail or having yours stepped on ends the game
CPU robot rivals (named after old machines) range further and chase your tail as rounds progress
eight boards, each cleared by exceeding a target percentage, ending in a 'King of Kings Tournament'
nine unlockable outfits bought with copper coins; the ground colour changes with the outfit
notes: Korean single-player paper.io-style game against bots, 1-3 minute rounds, 3D characters made in Blender.

title: Cartoon Kamasutra Xonix
notes: Known only from the No-Intro/libretro J2ME dat: one build, v1.0.0 (CRC FA07DF89). The title suggests an adult picture-reveal theme (which would fit adult-reveal), but the gameplay is undocumented.

title: Color Conquest
mechanics: connect dots to form enclosed shapes that claim territory in your colour
real-time simultaneous play against an AI with no turns, a live dots-and-boxes
enclosing shapes can steal the opponent's territory
notes: Distributed as a 56 MB APK on itch.io; tags include territory, ai, offline, competitive.

title: Hot Xonix (Palm OS)
notes: No-Intro lists 'Hot Xonix (USA) (Color)' (54,226-byte .prc) and '(Greyscale)' (34,983-byte .prc). The same DAT has Hot Pipes and Hot Worm in the same Color/Greyscale pairs. PalmDB's pages for Hot pipes and Hot lines link to palm-games.com, so Hot Xonix may belong to that 'Hot' series. This is unverified: the palm-games.com domain is now parked, and PalmDB has no Hot Xonix page.

title: Mobi Xonix 3D
notes: The J2ME dat lists 13 distinct v1.0 builds, which suggests wide handset and carrier distribution. A 3D presentation is implied only by the title.

title: mobiQix
notes: Known only from the No-Intro/libretro J2ME DAT: three dumps of 'mobiQix (www.ChumpChop.com) (1.0) (CLDC-1.0, MIDP-1.0)', with CRCs 097333B6, B1C520E2 and B9EB6F15. The vendor also made 'lottoChecker'. The lineage is inferred from the title only. chumpchop.com no longer resolves.

title: Pet Xonix
notes: Two builds (176x208 and 240x320) were uploaded to mobiles24 by the same user, with no description. The No-Intro J2ME dat lists a 'Pets ArtXonix' by VisualMedia (v1.0.1, MIDP-2.0) that may be the same game, but this is unconfirmed.

title: Qixxx
notes: Known only from the J2ME DAT entry 'Qixxx (Mediaplazza) (1.0) (CLDC-1.0, MIDP-1.0) (76BC1859)'. The same vendor string appears on ZooQix/ZooQuix, BrainSchool and BeachBabesMemory, and on some repacks. The lineage is inferred from the title. An adult theme is speculation from the title alone and is unconfirmed.

title: SimpleXonix
notes: A single v1.1 build (CRC A4966B7A) in the No-Intro/libretro J2ME dat. The listing gives only the title.

title: Xonix (Gergely Herenyi, J2ME)
notes: Versions 1.0.3 and 1.0.5 are in the J2ME dat. The author's contact is h.gergo@freemail.hu, a Hungarian freemail domain, and the same author has a J2ME Minesweeper. The listing gives only the title.

title: Xonix (Palm OS)
notes: No-Intro lists 'Xonix (USA)' as a 21,419-byte Xonix (USA).prc. No developer, year or description is recorded, and PalmDB has no matching page.

title: Xonix (Telma LTD, J2ME)
notes: A single v0.56 build (CRC 6A966C1E) in the No-Intro/libretro J2ME dat. The listing gives only the title.

title: Xonix Assault (Gameneeti, J2ME)
notes: The libretro J2ME DAT lists 11 builds of version 1.0 (jar sizes 110,902 to 710,615 bytes, i.e. per-handset builds) as 'Xonix Assault (Gameneeti) (1.0) (CLDC-1.1, MIDP-2.0)'. The same DAT also spells the company 'GameNeeti' on its many other J2ME titles. No gameplay description was found: gameneeti.com sits behind a bot check. A link to the Android 'Xonix Assault' (Digi10 Soft, 2016) is not established.

title: ZooQix
notes: The J2ME DAT lists 'ZooQix (Mediaplazza) (1.0)' (A84A690A) and 'ZooQuix (Mediaplazza) (1.0)' (D3D72C0A), both CLDC-1.0/MIDP-1.0. These are probably two spellings of one game. An animal theme is inferred from the title only.

title: quix (QIX on Unix)
developer: Unknown author of the original UNIX V7 C version. William 'Chomp' King ported it to CP/M (BDS C) in 1983/84. Anthony C. Howe (SirWumpus) later did a CP/M port (1985) and an Atari ST port, and maintains the source.
publisher: none (public domain; the GitHub mirror lists 0BSD)
mechanics: text-mode playfield with '@' as the player
the Qix kills only by crossing the open trail and cannot touch the player on the border; Sparx kill only on the border
a Fuse appears if the player stops off the border or crosses or doubles back on their own trail
bonus for each percent above 75%, and each new screen adds one more Qix
points for capturing a Qix by cutting it off from the others
extra man every 10,000 points
notes: The C source was found on a Sydney University machine and converted to CP/M in 1983/84. TOSEC lists 'Quix v2.0 (1986-09-25)(Howe, Anthony C.)(PD)' for the Atari ST. The repository moved from GitHub to Codeberg in Dec 2025. The README lists known bugs: a score rollover hang, and problems with 10 Qixes on screen.

title: Xonix (X11/Macintosh reimplementation)
developer: Torsten Schönitz (Mac original); Jörg Wunsch with Alfredo Herrera Hernández (X11)
mechanics: flyers bounce only in the unfilled area and kill by touching the player or the open trail; one more flyer each level
eaters also bounce across filled land and kill by touching the player; one more eater every fifth level
when the trail reaches filled land, the trail and every adjacent unfilled region with no flyer are filled
a level ends at 75% of the originally unfilled area
an extra life every second level
step timeout configurable (default 50 ms, 20 moves per second)
machine-wide top-ten score file; a compile-time option emails the previous leader when they lose first place
notes: A from-scratch remake of the PC/XT Xonix, started on the Mac and then ported to X11. The man page is dated 1995 (rev 1.7, 1995/08/28; copyright 1995 Joerg Wunsch). Debian packages it as 'xonix' 1.4 ('game to carve up the screen whilst dodging monsters'), with 1.5 in testing. Ubuntu Jammy has 1.4-34. The FreeBSD port was removed in 2016 and revived in April 2026 as v1.5, with the source moved to GitHub. No 'xqix' package was found.

title: IceBreaker
developer: Matthew Miller (Win32 port help from Enrico Tassi)
mechanics: bouncing penguins on an Antarctic iceberg replace the balls
a click starts two line halves growing in opposite directions; a penguin hitting a growing half removes it and costs a life (both halves = two lives)
clearing 80% of the iceberg completes the level
exponentially growing score bonus for clearing beyond 80%, plus a smaller bonus per remaining life
score drains by about one point per second while a level is played
each new iceberg adds one penguin and one life
deliberately letting a line break can leave small trap areas that make penguins easier to catch
notes: GPL-2.0-or-later. Written in sessions from September 2000 to May 2002; revived as 2.0 (August 2020) for Fedora, with 2.2.1 Windows builds in 2021. The author calls it a 'sort-of-clone' of JezzBall that deliberately does many things differently. Packaged in Debian (2.2.1). The TI-Nspire port nIceBreaker was uploaded to ticalc.org on 2013-12-20.

title: KBounce
developer: Stefan Schimanski (original author); KDE (KDE4 port and maintenance by Tomasz Boczkowski)
publisher: KDE (KDE Gear); Stefan Schimanski (App Store port)
mechanics: a left click starts two walls growing in opposite directions from the clicked square; a right click toggles the axis between horizontal and vertical
a ball hitting the body of a growing wall removes the whole new wall and costs a life
a ball meeting a wall's head head-on stops the wall there and makes it permanent with no life lost; hitting the head from another side just bounces
level n has n+1 balls, n+1 lives and a 30x(n+2) second time limit; running out of time ends the game
cover 75% of the field to clear; score is 15 points per remaining life plus a bonus from ball count and the share above 75%
the 2026 iOS port adds global leaderboards
notes: KDE's JezzBall clone. KAboutData credits Stefan Schimanski as original author (c) 2000-2005, with a KDE4 port by Tomasz Boczkowski (2007, packaged with KDE 4.0 in 2008). Licensed GPL-2.0-or-later and still released with KDE Gear (26.08.2, 2026-10-08). Windows and macOS builds are nightly test builds. Schimanski published a $0.99 iPhone/iPad/Mac version on the App Store in 2026.

title: Barrack (QBASIC)
mechanics: varied ball types, modelled on Ambrosia Software's Mac game Barrack (implied by the author's motivation; the types are not documented on the page)
configurable keyboard and mouse controls
notes: GPL-3.0 code. The author saw Ambrosia's Mac Barrack, had only a PC, and found JezzBall lacked Barrack's variety of ball types, so wrote this in QBASIC. Itch.io lists the release date as Jan 01, 2005, which looks like a year-only placeholder. Tag-page blurb: 'a QBASIC game I made a really long time ago'.

title: Xobox (Rockbox plugin)
mechanics: Xonix rules: the player leaves filled land to draw a trail, and on return every enclosed region with no qix is filled
starts with 2 bouncing qixes and adds one per level; levels stop at 10 (12 qixes at most)
the fill target is a menu setting from 5% to 95% in steps of 5 (default 75%)
speed setting from 1 to 10 (loop period (11-speed)*10 ms)
a qix touching the open trail erases the trail, sends the player back to the start and costs one of 3 lives
each level clear adds the filled percentage to the score; top-5 high scores
a game in progress can be saved and resumed from the menu
notes: Rules read from the GPL source (constants STARTING_QIXES 2, MAX_LEVEL 10, difficulty 75, speed 6). The Rockbox wiki page blocked automated access.

title: Xonix (KolibriOS)
mechanics: two enemy kinds: at level n, n+1 balls bounce in the unclaimed area and n balls bounce over claimed land; land balls kill only when the player is on land with no trail, unclaimed-area balls kill by touching the trail or the player while a trail is open
the clear condition is a remaining-cell budget that grows with the enemy count: the level ends when unclaimed cells fall to 30 x (level+1) + level

catch-up pickups appear at random on claimed land: a red bonus (fewer than 3 lives, over 50% done) gives a life, and a green bonus (fewer than 2 lives, over 75% done) gives 250 ticks in which the player passes through enemies and eats them for 100 points each
an extra life at the start of a level if the previous level was cleared without dying
field size adjustable from 48x28 to 96x56 cells in steps of 2 (default 64x32)
score per claimed cell (trail included); top-10 table with 12-character names saved to xonix.t10
notes: C++ source in the KolibriOS repository (programs/games/xonix), window title 'XONIX (C) MMVI by Rabid Rabbit'. Ships with KolibriOS 0.7.7.0. Starts with 3 lives. A flip animation plays between levels.

title: BobBall
mechanics: infinite levels
local top-scores table
notes: 'A simple free/libre and open-source version of the old game JezzBall for Android.' BSD-2-Clause. First added to the F-Droid repository on 2015-07-28. Later versions: 1.14 (Jan 2016), 1.15 (Feb 2016), 1.17 (Aug 2024).

title: Assorted open-source tutorial clones
mechanics: a terminal play field sized by the window, styled like an old green text terminal (CheshirCa/Xonix, Python curses)
enemies move in linear, zig-zag or circular patterns; local 2-player; a Continuous mode adds enemies over time (tahreem7926/Xonix)
a 3-second time-freeze power-up; 2-player co-op or competition in which crossing the other player's trail is a collision; a bonus for 10 or more tiles in one capture (KanwalAi)
Pac-Xon style: a destroyer enemy erases claimed tiles, and a hunter chases the player while off land (Eques72/Xonix)
claimed area reveals a pet picture, 80% to clear (VladaMamutova/PetsArtXoniX)
a 50-level Godot 4 Android JezzBall remake: swipe to start a wall, 70% target, level N has N atoms and max(3, N+2) lives, restart refills lives (Matswm86/jezzball)
notes: The long tail of student and learning projects: Pyxel (Boundarpy, DrIce99/qix), Scala/LibGDX (qixxy, a 2016 university project), V/wasm (vixanix), SFML/SDL2 C++ Xonix assignments, PowerShell (uludice/xonips), Kotlin (lure0xaos/Xenox), PureBasic (CheshirCa/Xonix-PB), and JezzBalls in Tkinter (armanelgtron) and Three.js (mikezupper/containment, 3D). The lineage is mixed: mostly Xonix, plus some Qix and JezzBall clones. The vixanix README credits the 1984 MS-DOS Xonix to Ilan Rav and Dani Katz. The Matswm86 README says Entertainment Pack 3, but Wikipedia lists JezzBall in Pack 4. The topic pages list further leads I did not check: azartsov/photo-slice-native (levels cut from device photos), Nomadjackalope/caffeinatedsheep (sheep herding with JezzBall walls), SirWumpus/quix (*nix), EgonOlsen71/Kidelyneen (Commodore BASIC V2), newagebegins/xonix-pico8, raulbojalil Wii U and 3DS JezzBall ports, and ronaldstoner/jezzball-nes.

title: qixxy
mechanics: fast draw plus a slow draw at 0.3x speed; slow-drawn areas get their own colour and are scored separately
goal: fence off a 'supermajority' of the playfield
a difficulty setting changes the ship's speed
polygon-based playfield: claimed areas are vector polygons, not grid cells
notes: A straight QIX clone in Scala/LibGDX with Qix, Spark, Fuse, lives and score objects. The README says it was 'written as a university project in 2016' and is no longer maintained. It is MIT-licensed, and the README's clone URL points to oeshiro/qixxy.

title: kux.io
mechanics: online multiplayer Splix.io-style territory game on self-hostable Node.js servers
players pick a name and colour and join a server by URL
notes: Self-described 'A splix.io clone' and '2D snake-like RTS game'; Apache-2.0. Commits run from 30 Sep 2017 to Jan 2019. The README to-do list still shows features such as land claiming and collisions as open, although a floodfill.js is present, so I could not confirm how complete it is.

title: caffeinatedsheep
mechanics: the bouncing hazards are sheep to be caught: build fences to pen them, and sheep break fences that are not finished in time
coins from caught sheep buy food (attracts sheep) or dogs (repels them), placed on the field to herd sheep and open space for fences
score goal: catch the most sheep, not reach an area percentage
notes: MIT-licensed libGDX project with four commits, all on 14 August 2018. The JezzBall link comes only from the repo's 'jezzball' topic tag; the README does not name JezzBall. Platform folders exist, but which platforms are complete is not stated.

title: Boundarpy
publisher: none (source on GitHub; license not stated)
mechanics: one bouncing enemy and no Sparx or Fuse
the player leaves the border only by moving perpendicular to it, into the field
the enemy touching the line being drawn ends the game (one life)
win by boxing the enemy in until it can no longer move, not by reaching a percentage target
keyboard or gamepad, with instant restart
notes: A small Pyxel QIX-style game (210x160) described as 'QIX-style territory capture game built with Python and Pyxel'. The repo has 35 commits and was last updated 9 Nov 2019. It has no README. The rules above come from reading main.py: the game is 'CLEAR' once the enemy stays still for 30 frames, and a code comment marks fill and percentage calculation as not implemented.

title: PetsArtXoniX
mechanics: claimed area reveals a hidden pet picture; 80% clears the round and shows the whole picture, with a different picture each round
enemies hitting the trail cost a life, and so does the player's own ball crossing its own trail
lives do not refill between rounds; losing them all restarts the game
settings for the number of enemies, ball speed and lives, plus a sound toggle
results saved under a player name
notes: A C++/Windows API student project with a Russian README. Commits run from December 2019 to January 2, 2020.

title: Corbynball
publisher: Liam O'Connor (self-published on itch.io, name your own price)
mechanics: three selectable speed settings
Micro Mode: the game uses only a small part of the screen and can be shown at half size on high-DPI displays
notes: Part of the 'Micro Entertainment Pack' of tiny desktop games, written in Rust with SDL2 and SDL_gfx. Code is BSD-3-Clause and assets are CC0, with source in github.com/liamoc/desktop_games. Its diagonal-only balls that bounce off each other are faithful to JezzBall, not new. The year is from the earliest dated item, a devlog of 25 Jan 2020, so the first release may be earlier.

title: xonix-js
notes: A straight clone: a tiny MIT-licensed JavaScript canvas clone of the classic Xonix. It can be played on itch.io and at michelebucelli.github.io/xonix-js. Commits run from January 13, 2020 to January 16, 2021.

title: Quick Impulse Xpansion
mechanics: freehand path drawn by holding the left mouse button from the screen border, instead of moving a marker in four directions
the hazard is lava, not a Qix
the captured area is computed with GDevelop's Marching Squares (scalar field) extension; press D to show the hit-boxes
notes: An entry to VIDEO GAMES LAB: Game Jam 2021, with MIT-licensed code that opens in the GDevelop online editor. The title's initials spell QIX. A post-jam update fixed path drawing, the completion calculation and double-counted deaths.

title: Xonix (Pac-Man hybrid, Eques72)
mechanics: a destroyer enemy bounces diagonally and erases inner claimed tiles it bounces off (the outer border is safe)
a hunter enemy spawns in the middle of the map and chases the player in straight lines while the player is off claimed land, then goes back to its spawn point once the player is on land
the destroyer and hunter play alongside default bouncing enemies
notes: The README calls it a 'variation of game xonix mixed with pac-man style' ('Pac-xon version'), made to learn C++20, SFML and multithreading. Full HD only. Commits date from April to June 2022. The enemy behaviour was read from DestroyerEnemy.cpp and HunterEnemy.cpp.

title: vixanix
notes: A straight clone: an MIT-licensed remake of Xonix in V, with a wasm/HTML build (wasm_embeds.v, vixanix.html). The README credits the 1984 MS-DOS original to Ilan Rav and Dani Katz and an Apple II port (1986) to Orlin Shopov. Commits are dated September 1 to 7, 2025.

title: Xonix-Game-Development-Project / xonic-game-cpp-sfml
developer: KanwalAi (Kanwal Fatima, Ayesha Faryal); Dawood3838 (Muhammad Dawood)
mechanics: two players on one keyboard, either cooperating or competing for space; crossing the other player's trail counts as a collision (KanwalAi)
Continuous mode: one more enemy every 30 seconds and a speed increase every 20 seconds (KanwalAi)
a power-up key freezes enemies and the opponent for 3 seconds (KanwalAi)
bonus points for capturing 10 or more tiles in one move (KanwalAi)
enemies move in circular and zig-zag patterns (KanwalAi)
power-ups are earned at score milestones and give temporary advantages; score, time and moves are tracked (Dawood3838)
notes: Two separate Programming Fundamentals course projects, grouped together. KanwalAi's is marked Fall 2025 and was pushed in February 2026. Dawood3838's is from FAST NUCES Islamabad and was pushed in June 2026. Both have Easy/Medium/Hard and Continuous modes, and they share most features with tahreem7926/Xonix, which suggests a common assignment.

title: Containment
mechanics: 3D-lit chamber (Three.js) over a deterministic 2D rules engine at 120 fixed ticks per second
walls grow in two halves; a ball hitting a growing half breaks only that half and costs a life, and a completed half stays
claim 75% of the chamber before time or lives run out; each new chamber adds a ball
keyboard aim with a 4-cell fast move, plus mouse and touch placement
Slow pace option
notes: Independent MIT-licensed project inspired by the 1992 Windows JezzBall. TypeScript with Vite and the Gyral action framework. First commits on 8 October 2026. Its fixed-tick deterministic design is directly comparable to Jiro-ikusu's.

title: Ink Fill
platforms: Browser (single self-contained HTML file; mouse and touch)
mechanics: instead of steering a marker, the player drags and releases to launch a ball that bounces off walls; its trail seals off enemy-free areas
an unfinished trail can be broken by enemies and must be protected until it closes
'tool marbles' hit by the ball freeze, move or defeat enemies
52 stages in 7 worlds, each with its own coverage target; later stages add terrain combinations and boss fights
stars for finishing a stage in fewer shots, which rewards planned shots over volume
notes: MIT-licensed. Made with AI (Codex and Claude) under human direction; the author released the source because they could not make it as fun as they wanted. A billiards-style take on area capture. Stages are generated offline with route search and replay verification against the game's own simulation, which is relevant to a deterministic core.

title: JezzBall (Matswm86 Godot Android remake)
platforms: Desktop (run from source in the Godot editor)
mechanics: swipe gestures replace mouse clicks to launch a horizontal or vertical wall
70% of the field must be walled off to clear a level, where Microsoft's JezzBall needs 75%
level N has N atoms and max(3, N+2) lives; 50 levels, then the game loops back to level 1
a RESTART button replays the current level with lives refilled
notes: Faithful remake of the 1992 Microsoft Entertainment Pack 3 game in Godot 4.6 (GDScript, single scene). It has procedurally drawn Windows 3.x-style graphics and no ads, purchases, tracking or Android permissions. Sound, menus, saves and high scores are not implemented yet. Releases (v0.5.0 and a rolling build, dated 2 May) are debug-signed sideload APKs. The year is inferred from Godot 4.6 and repository activity (last updated October 2026). The repository states no licence, so it is source-available rather than formally open source.

title: looprush
mechanics: online multiplayer: rooms of up to 16 members, matches of up to 8 players started by the host once all are ready; no bots
continuous movement on a square board (48 to 384 cells, default 256), steered by cardinal keys or a free heading with a turn-rate limit
heart-shaped starting territory at a random spawn kept a minimum distance from other players
returning home flood-fills from the board edges: every cell unreachable from the edge becomes yours
a cell claimed by two players in the same tick becomes neutral
you die by leaving the board, hitting your own trail, having your trail cut (the cutter gets the kill, split among several cutters), a head-on collision or swapped cells, or 12 s without input
pickups spawn every 3 s, up to 18: speed (1.6x for 5 s), shield (new trail uncuttable for 3 s), frost (rivals within 14 cells slowed to 0.55x for 3 s), teleport (resets dash cooldown)
dash ability: 4x speed for 0.18 s on a 12 s cooldown, usable only while not drawing a trail
no timer: the match ends when nobody is alive; score is peak board share, points are owned cells plus 100 per kill
accounts, top-20 leaderboard, last-10 match history and uploaded face-image avatars
notes: Python server with a TypeScript/Vite client, run via Docker Compose; MIT licence. Initial release 2 Oct 2026. The README warns of sexual innuendo in its theme and interface. A 'radar' pickup is declared but has no effect in server.py.

title: Paper Loop
mechanics: grid-based movement, square by square in four directions
leaving your territory draws a trail; closing it back into your territory claims the enclosed ground
running over a rival's trail knocks it out; your own trail is your weak spot
sealing a rival's trail inside your capture also eliminates it
opponents are on-device neural bots trained by self-play, plus a hand-written scripted bot
live minimap and local high score
notes: GPL-3.0-only libGDX game; version 1.0.0 added to F-Droid on 4 July 2026. Fully offline, no accounts, ads or tracking.

title: Paper Loop 2
mechanics: free continuous steering with a real heading and gradual turns instead of grid steps
circular arena; steering too steeply into the wall eliminates you
loop out from your territory and close a shape to claim the area inside
slicing a rival's tail knocks it out; your own tail is your weak spot
opponent modes: AI HARD (self-play trained net), EASY SCRIPTED or NO BOTS; optional respawn toggle
local high score per mode
notes: Free-movement sequel to Paper Loop; GPL-3.0-only libGDX game, first F-Droid version 1.0.1 added 5 July 2026. Fully offline.

title: Photo Slice
mechanics: each level's hidden image is a random photo from the device's own media library (demo backdrop when access is denied)
tap-to-steer cursor: a tap launches the cut into the image, then each tap turns it 90 degrees toward the tapped side
closing a cut reveals the SMALLER of the two areas instead of the side without the enemy
hazards caught inside a revealed area are removed; clearing all hazards opens the whole photo and the run continues with a new photo
a hazard touching the open cut fails the attempt
five difficulties set the hazard count: Sunny 3, Cloudy 4, Stormy 5, Blizzard 6, Apocalypse 8; per-difficulty counters of opened photos
notes: Public GitHub prototype (TypeScript, Expo, EAS builds for APK/AAB), described as inspired by Xonix; repo topics include xonix. Commits run from July to September 2026. No license is shown on the repository page, so it is public source rather than clearly open-source. Its 'reveal the smaller side' rule replaces Qix's 'side without the boss' rule.

title: Territory Raider
mechanics: shield mode: invulnerable while walking the claimed border; hold Space to draw into the dark
flood fill from the boss: the side holding the boss stays dark, everything else is claimed
Sparks race along the open trail toward the player; touching an enemy or being reached by a spark costs a life and rolls the trail back
minions chase the player; enclosing them destroys them for a trap bonus
60-second timer per life: enemies speed up +25% at 20 s and +50% at 10 s left; time-out costs a life
boss fight every 5 stages: aimed shots on cooldown, faster above 40% claimed, 3-shot spreads above 65%; shots vanish on claimed land, which works as cover; the boss only wanders on other stages
power-up tiles collected by enclosing them: T time stop, S speed, L laser charge, P score, C clear minions
laser (X) fired from shield mode: hitting the boss instantly claims the whole field with a large bonus
from stage 2, unclaimable rock clusters block trails and enemy shots and are excluded from the 80% target

from stage 11, fire, ice and lightning themes rotate every 10 stages: fire burns the trail back and must be surrounded; ice halves speed for 3 s and makes you slide; lightning freezes you for 1 s but stuns nearby minions for 2.5 s; enclosing a hazard patch removes it
endless stages with an 80% clear target
notes: A React 18, TypeScript and Canvas 2D homage to Volfied and Qix, with a headless pure-TypeScript engine (fixed 60 Hz step, 116 Vitest tests) and Electron desktop builds. First commits June 2026; v0.1.0 to v0.3.0 released 17 July 2026. The README says the name, art and sound are original. The hazard patches and the boss shots that vanish on claimed land map directly onto a boss-and-minions design.

title: BlocklyIO
mechanics: Paper.io clone (trail out of your territory, loop back to enclose land)
sets out to add real online multiplayer, which the single-player-vs-bots Paper.io lacked; the README calls it a demo
notes: MIT-licensed Node.js project, 51 stars and 74 forks. The README calls it a clone of Voodoo's Paper.io 'except for one aspect': multiplayer.

title: jezzball-kazzmir
mechanics: walls covering 80% of the screen clear the level
each level adds one extra life and one more ball
left click builds a wall, right click toggles its direction
notes: Allegro 4 rewrite of JezzBall, first made for Windows and later lightly ported to Linux. Packaged as v1.1 on SlackBuilds.org (Slackware 14.2), which calls it 'a classic game much like qix'; the packaging includes an extra-backgrounds tarball and an insults.diff patch whose effect is undocumented.

title: Boxer Rebellion
mechanics: fill pre-set score boxes by tracing their complete outline while avoiding enemies (box outlining rather than free-form Qix cuts)
nine levels
notes: Freeware. DOSGames.com and AbandonwareDOS file it as a Qix-style game, but the box-outlining goal is closer to Amidar. The DOSGames reviewer says it differs enough from Qix to be more engaging. The zip also includes BOXERPT2.EXE, which skips the title screen.

title: QIX (Bartlein & Chin, DOS)
mechanics: gameplay details unknown (dat listing only: QIX.EXE, genre Action)
notes: An independent DOS QIX (QIX.EXE, 46,080 bytes) listed in libretro's DOS.dat with year 1985 and developer 'R. Bartlein, S. Chin'. It is separate from the Taito-credited 1989 Qix entries in the same dat.

title: Gapper
developer: unknown (no credit in the executable; the libretro DOS database lists "Anonymous")
mechanics: grid line painting: walk the player (Gapper) over the blue lines of a rectangular grid to turn every line red; the screen is cleared when all lines are coloured (Amidar model)
box capture scoring: 50 points for each grid square whose four sides are all red; 100 points for enclosing a flashing extra-point box while it is lit
temporary gap: Space or Return cuts a short-lived gap in the lines that neither the player nor the enemy can cross, used to shake off the pursuer; each gap costs 5 points
single pursuer (the Seeker) that takes the shortest route to intercept the player; it starts in the opposite corner (player top left, Seeker bottom right)
level ramp: each level speeds up the Seeker, shortens the gap duration and adds more boxes to the grid
lives: 2 extra men at the start, plus 1 every 5000 points
notes: IBM PC game compiled from BASIC with the IBM BASIC Compiler (the executable carries the IBM runtime banner). The rules above come from the game's own instruction screen, read from the strings in GAPPER.EXE. Wikipedia's article on it was deleted in 2015 as a "non-notable, freeware clone" of Amidar, after an AfD in which MobyGames was the best source anyone found. The Internet Archive's MS-DOS library has it as msdos_Gapper_1986, with a MobyGames-derived description. The gap mechanic, a temporary wall the player drops behind them that blocks the pursuer, is the game's own twist.

title: Cobweb
mechanics: a second enemy type moves outside the open field and kills on contact, alongside the diagonal bouncers inside it
a countdown timer runs to the end of the session
a bonus makes the trail temporarily invulnerable to enemies
theme: the player is a spider webbing over a garbage bin with flies inside, while a garbage spider-eater named Domino hunts it
levels grow harder as they progress
notes: Soviet freeware Xonix clone. old-games.ru gives the origin as domestic (Soviet/Russian) and Ukraine, with Russian and English text. It has CGA graphics with switchable palettes and PC-speaker sound. The game is speed-sensitive and barely playable on anything faster than a 286.

title: Kicks
mechanics: 70% capture target to advance
three enemy types to avoid or wall off: Rollers, Suiveurs (followers) and the Kicks
notes: A French-language Qix variant that the old-games.ru review says differs very little from Qix. Its year is 1989 in both old-games.ru and libretro's DOS.dat (KICKS.COM).

title: Araña
mechanics: 90% capture target instead of 75%
a single enemy patrols the border, so the border is not a safe zone and that enemy cannot be trapped
field enemies start at three and gain one per level; you can isolate them in prepared pockets so the rest fills more easily
retracing your path or crossing your own trail costs a life
larger single captures score more; extra life every 3,000 points
one of four difficulty levels, fixed at launch, sets the enemy count (up to six) and the speed of both player and enemies
notes: The old-games.ru review calls it a Spanish remake of Xonix. libretro's DOS.dat lists it as ARAÑA (ARANA.COM) by PC Disc with no year. Whether it was shareware is unconfirmed.

title: Ballistyx
mechanics: bouncing balls in the open field plus enemies that travel along tracks
adjustable player, ball and enemy speeds, with score multipliers by difficulty
graphical level editor: draw the playfield, tracks and obstacles; place balls, enemies and the player; validate and test before saving; import and export levels as PNG images
user-made levels alongside the built-in ones
notes: Written in the 1990s while the author learned DirectX. The itch page claims over 1,000,000 downloads and appearances on commercial compilation discs. It was later 'completely rewritten for macOS and iOS'. V1.10 is built from the original C++ source for modern Windows and sold pay-what-you-want (minimum £1).

title: 陣取りゲーム (Matsuo & Takagi)
developer: 松尾啓志 (Hiroshi Matsuo), 高木浩光 (Hiromitsu Takagi)
mechanics: programming game: each player writes a program that controls several 'bugs' instead of steering by hand
moving bugs draw trails on the field, and any closed region formed by a player's trails becomes that player's territory
score is the total enclosed area
notes: Freeware. The v2.00 archive (jintori.lzh) is dated 1990-12-10 and the v2.01 executable-only archive (jin201ex.lzh) 1991-04-01. The '2.00' suggests an earlier version existed. Vector files it under Board Games.

title: Mamba
mechanics: the player is a spider spinning webs; the only enemy is one long snake that moves fast at right angles and tends to chase the spider
the snake crossing your unfinished web erases only that web, without a kill
the snake touching the spider costs a life, erases the web and resets the spider to the top-left corner; captured areas stay
on closing a web, the spider gets the part of the field the snake is not in
80% target; three lives that cannot be restored
no level time limit, but each capture after the first has a 30-second allowance, which counters waiting for the snake to wander into a trap (the penalty for exceeding it is not described)
notes: The old-games.ru review calls it a Xonix variant. Data Becker was a commercial German publisher, so pc-shareware is the nearest category, not an exact fit.

title: JezzBall
platforms: Windows (The Best of Microsoft Entertainment Pack re-release)
mechanics: no edge-walking avatar: the player clicks anywhere to start a horizontal or vertical wall that grows both ways from the pointer; right-click switches orientation
atoms bounce around the room; an atom touching a wall still being built stops it and costs a life
a wall that reaches the edges unbroken fills every region with no atom
capture at least 75% of the room within a time limit
level 1 has 2 atoms and each level adds one; from level 49 on, every level has 50
lives at the start of a level equal the number of atoms
notes: A commercial title in Microsoft Entertainment Pack 4, not shareware. It is filed as pc-shareware because that is the closest PC category, as the root of the JezzBall family. It was re-released in The Best of Microsoft Entertainment Pack and was on Microsoft's Gamesampler disk. It was not in the Game Boy Color or Windows CE Entertainment Pack releases. atsb/JezzBall is a separate 64-bit reverse-engineered port of the Windows 3.1 release for Windows 10/11.

title: Mamba 2
mechanics: ten selectable starting levels: level 1 starts with pre-built web sections, level 10 starts with no web and three fast snakes
option to reveal a full-screen picture in claimed areas instead of the plain grey web pattern

(inherited from Mamba 1991, which Mamba 2 updates mostly cosmetically) a snake that crosses an unfinished web line erases only that line; touching the spider costs one of three lives and sends it back to the top-left corner, while claimed areas stay
(inherited from Mamba 1991) the snake moves fast on right-angled paths and tends to chase the spider
(inherited from Mamba 1991) 80% capture target; no level timer, but each further capture must be made within 30 seconds
notes: Mostly cosmetic update of Mamba (1991): brighter palette, menus (Hilfe/Spiel/Optionen), optional sound, resettable high-score table. Theme: a spider spinning web against snakes. Data Becker is a commercial German publisher; the source does not state whether it was sold or distributed as shareware.

title: Gotcha
mechanics: 50% claim threshold to advance (instead of Qix's 75%)
enemies ('meanies') include a bouncing wavy-line creature
mouse control as an alternative to the arrow keys
+ and - keys change the game speed during play
notes: The shareware version has 5 levels. A few options can be set before starting.

title: VGA Kix
mechanics: two-player mode on one computer (per old-games.ru; DOSGames.com lists the game as single-player)
notes: Straight Qix clone: a roaming multicoloured Kix that must not touch the stylus or the line being drawn, and two sparks (blue dots) that run along the borders and finished lines. Alt speeds the stylus up and Ctrl slows it down, and slow cuts are riskier but score more, as in Qix. Highly configurable settings and built-in help with strategy tips. Freeware; the author sold the source code for a fee. Archive vgakix15.zip (v1.5).

title: 陣取り (Evio)
mechanics: the player (a light-blue dot) grows its own territory: leaving it lays a yellow line, and returning adds the enclosed part
the only enemy is a red snake moving diagonally; touching it kills, and so does the snake touching the player or the yellow line
red line segments appear at random times, places and lengths; touching one kills, and so does one striking the player or the yellow line
the big red outer frame kills on contact, so moving along the wall needs careful key handling
enclosing the snake ends the round as a win: every part of the screen without the snake becomes the player's

scoring ignores the share of area claimed: 100 fixed hidden points on a 10x10 grid each score 1 if covered by territory or the yellow line when the round ends (by death or by enclosing the snake), so memorising their positions is the route to 100
notes: Japanese freeware. Vector lists version 1.1 as quick3.lzh (36,993 bytes) dated 1993-11-20.

title: Strong Lines
mechanics: claimed sections are cut out of digitized city-landscape backgrounds
more enemy balls (white dots) are added as the player progresses
per-level timer (100 s on level 1); running out costs a life
four difficulty settings that differ in the fill percentage needed to advance
notes: Shareware distributed on the cover CDs of gaming and computer magazines. Three lives, no saves.

title: Y
mechanics: an enemy ball patrols the claimed border (like Qix's Sparx) alongside the ball bouncing in the open field; both grow in number and speed as the game progresses
a level is cleared by claiming at least 75% of the field
each level has a three-minute time limit
temporary bonuses appear in the open field for a while, among them instant level clear, destroy enemies and extra life
notes: Small Xonix variant in English, tagged W.I.S.E. (under 100 KB) on old-games.ru. Its license is not stated.

title: Hidden Fields
mechanics: claimed boxes uncover a hidden picture; the DOSGames.com reviewer identifies the pictures as Frank Frazetta fantasy paintings
14 enemy types, with different enemies on each level
90% claim target (per FILE_ID.DIZ)
four difficulty levels
