notes: 256-colour graphics, over 40 sound effects, Sound Blaster support. The FILE_ID.DIZ line 'If you can get 90 percent back of your field, you won one of 28 !' does not say what the 28 are (pictures or prizes). LOMAX also published Lovely Girls (1998).

title: Barrack
mechanics: a shooter fires walls across the field to fence in bouncing balls (JezzBall rules), instead of an edge-walking marker drawing lines
several ball types that behave differently; a fan remake's author names this variety as its main difference from JezzBall
notes: Released March 8, 1996 (nextquest). Wikipedia's infobox credits Greg Lovette as developer and lists the game under Ambrosia Software's published titles. Macworld's Cosmo Bots review uses it as a reference point. No accessible source describes the individual ball types. The Obscuritory's article, which Wikipedia cites, could not be reached from this session.

title: Queeks
alt_titles: ヘビを閉じ込める陣取りゲーム
mechanics: the goal is to enclose the roaming snake enemies inside your territory plus your expedition line, instead of reaching a percentage
with several snakes on screen, all of them must be enclosed at the same time to clear the stage
your territory is coloured yellow and green, and touching any other colour on the field kills you
notes: Japanese shareware, version 1.01 (queek101.lzh, 291,247 bytes, dated 1996-09-25 on Vector), with a three-week trial and a current price of 1,210 yen. The Vector tagline reads 'a territory-capture game where you shut in snakes'. Evio also made the MS-DOS game 陣取り. The lineage is the cataloguer's call: the description uses territory plus an expedition line, as in Xonix.

title: Squarex
mechanics: capture grid squares by going along all four sides (grid capture instead of free cuts)
levels are timed
orange cubes chase the player around the grid
reaching a pink cube turns the tables: the player can then capture the orange cubes (a Pac-Man-style power-up)
notes: DOSGames.com describes it as a 'strange cross between Pac-Man and Qix' and says it is 'tougher than it looks'. Single-player.

title: Super Xonix
mechanics: a full picture shows at the start and each claimed area covers part of it, the reverse of the usual Qix reveal
optional 2-player mode against a friend (stated in the bundled FILE_ID.DIZ; the DOSGames metadata says single player)
notes: Freeware 256-colour VGA (320x200) remake of DOS Xonix, dated 'JAN 96' in its FILE_ID.DIZ, needs a 286. The enemies are ordinary bouncing balls, as in base Xonix. DOSGames contradicts itself on multiplayer: its metadata says single player, while the DIZ says '1-2 PLAYERS' and 'play alone or against a friend'.

title: Coach Tzabar
mechanics: clearing the field reveals a hidden picture (landscapes, vegetable still lifes); the target is usually 70%, varying by level
the player is safe on the border even if touched; Space must be held to leave it and draw into the field
dying loses the current cut only; cleared sections stay; lives are limited for the whole game

on medium and hard, bonus boxes appear briefly and block movement; cut so the box sits on the new border, it bursts and its item must be collected: temporary speed, freeze monsters, or destroy all small monsters (no boxes on easy)
on easy a trapped monster prevents its area from clearing; on hard trapped monsters self-destruct
hard difficulty adds a large toothy monster that roams the field with long jumps; medium and hard add a strict time limit
clearing more than required can award an extra life
notes: An Israeli Hebrew-language advergame in which the player is a cactus wizard. Old-Games.ru calls it Xonix-like, and Hebrew Wikipedia lists it among games inspired by Xonix. Its item boxes (speed, freeze, kill small monsters) and self-destructing trapped monsters echo Volfied.

title: Prometheus
notes: Listed only as 'Prometheus/Qrax (1997, Mac, Quarter Note Software)' in Wikipedia's Qix clone list, with no citation. No gameplay details found.

title: Xonix32
mechanics: Android version: swipe anywhere on the screen to set the player's direction
Android version: black rectangular 'black holes' on the board are sealed and vanish when enclosed with no enemy inside (absent from Classic mode)
claim at least 75% of the area
notes: Shelvely lists Xonix32 as a freeware Windows remake of DOS Xonix released 5 July 1997, with no developer named. GythaOgg's Android game (released 15 Dec 2013, last updated 9 Jun 2015) says it 'originally started as an android version of the classic game Xonix32'. A second listing, 'Xonix32' (gythaogg.gamesplus.xonix32), was updated in Nov 2020. In both, enemies move diagonally at constant speed and bounce off obstacles, as in base Xonix. The swipe and black-hole mechanics are documented only for the Android version.

title: AirXonix
publisher: AxySoft; eGames; Greenstreet Software; X3D Technologies
mechanics: isometric 3D field; the player is a spinning helicopter-like craft flying above it
mines roam the already-claimed area and kill on contact
striped balls destroy territory you have already claimed
spiked balls roll over claimed land and block level completion
collectible bonuses: extra life, extra score, extra time, temporary slowdown of all balls and mines, plus speed-up/slow-down modifiers
each level has a time limit
5 game types and 80+ levels; higher difficulty settings add more stages
shareware trial is limited until registered
notes: Russian 3D Xonix remake. MyAbandonware and BestOldGames give a 2000 worldwide release; old-games.ru, TASVideos and Wikidata say 2001. It had US/UK retail releases in 2001 and 2003. AxySoft's own page lists an iPhone/iPad version released 8 Sep 2015, which is no longer in the App Store catalogue. The 'Delico Games' credit comes from a separate Android remake, 'Air Xonix: Remastered' (Play package com.DelicoGames.Xonix, developer account 'Andrii Serba', first released Dec 2020), which is 'inspired by' the 2001 PC game and adds Episodes, Challenge levels and Daily Events.

title: Bolyx
mechanics: three colour stages in sequence (blue, then green, then red); each must be restored before the next
Space bar reverses the direction of the bouncing balls
bonus points for every percent filled beyond 75%
notes: Freeware Visual Basic 6 remake of Firebird's 1987 C64 game Zolyx, which GB64 calls a Qix clone. The bundled Bolyx.txt reads 'Bolyx by James Burrows, Version 1.1, 24 October 2001, Copyright 2001 Waterbiscuit Games'. Also adds a storyline and a high-score saver, neither of which is gameplay. GB64 points to a 'vastly superior' new version, Trappy Pixel. That is a separate game (2023, agent4125, Godot; Windows, Mac, Linux and browser) and should get its own entry. It adds 4 difficulty levels, 1- and 2-player modes, a 90-second level timer whose expiry spawns more enemy pixels, and Reverse power-ups.

title: Discovera
platforms: PC (operating system not stated; distributed through download catalogs)
developer: Igor and Dmitry Bukhman (later founders of Playrix)
notes: The Bukhman brothers' first game, which Wikipedia says was similar to Xonix. They uploaded it to about 200 software catalogs, sold it for $15, and earned about $60 in the first month. Qixote calls it a series; I found no source for later entries.

title: Panic (Y.O.S.)
mechanics: enclose a masked area while avoiding enemies; capturing 80% of the masked area clears the stage
a bonus stage after every three stages; 16 stages in total (13 regular and 3 bonus)
notes: Japanese freeware (フリーソフト), labelled 陣取りゲーム (territory-capture game). The Vector download is Panic 1.0, panic20020701.lzh, dated 2002.07.01.

title: Space Xonix
mechanics: enemies are presented as mines in an alien minefield (theme; from a database summary only)
notes: Not the 2015 Steam game of the same name (the Qixote wiki notes two unrelated Space Xonix games, from 2002 and 2015). Retro Replay's genre metadata looks MobyGames-derived (Action/Arcade/Puzzle, sci-fi) and credits MobyGames for screenshots. MobyGames itself was blocked (403). Retro Replay's long text is generic and looks machine-written. Its claims of chasing mine variants, multiplayer, timed runs and optional objectives are unsupported and have been removed.

title: Cartoon Xonix
mechanics: player cuts a trail (a chain of dots) from the claimed area into the covered area; closing the trail claims the enclosed region
each claimed region uncovers part of a full-screen cartoon background picture, with a 'Revealed %' counter in the HUD
enemies roam both the covered area and the already-revealed area, as in Xonix
a different cartoon picture on each level (level 12 seen in screenshots), with score, level and lives HUD
notes: AG.ru (RAWG data) lists it as an arcade game for PC by Arcade Games Download, released 10 May 2004, with the developer page http://www.arcade-game-download.com/cartoon-xonix.php (the domain no longer resolves). I checked the mechanics against the two AG.ru screenshots: a trail drawn into a hatched covered area, 'REVEALED: 51 %' and '90 %' counters, and enemies on both kinds of area. The level-12 picture shows Disney-style characters, probably used without a licence. The Qixote fan wiki spells it 'Cartoon Xionix'. The earlier Softpedia snippet said the player drives a small train, that there are many bonuses and that the unregistered version locks some levels. The player sprite and dotted trail look like a small train, but I could not confirm any of the three claims because Softpedia returns 403. They stay out of the mechanics list.

title: Cosmic Bugs
mechanics: carve the field with dividing lines to claim a required share; enemies trapped in a closed area are destroyed
enemies on the border shoot at the player while a line is being drawn
most enemies move randomly, but some track the cursor to block lines
destroyed enemies can drop power-ups (missiles, bombs, line enhancers) or power-downs that make play harder
notes: Released November 11, 2004 (LaunchBox), with a space theme. LaunchBox calls it a take on Qix and JezzBall. It is the predecessor of Water Bugs. It is very likely the Windows name of Cosmo Bots: same developer, same year, and the same enemies and drops. The GameSpot review returned 403, so a PopCap Games publisher credit and the 'fake power-ups' detail could not be checked.

title: Cosmo Bots
mechanics: instead of drawing with an edge-walking marker, a shooter fires beams that grow into walls; a key switches them between vertical and horizontal
fill 85% of the frame to clear a level
enemies inside an enclosed area are destroyed, and destroyed enemies sometimes drop power-ups
power-ups: fast shot, enemy slow motion, score multipliers, time bombs, missiles and bombs, line enhancers
power-downs: slower shooter, faster enemies, shorter line, inverted controls
some enemies track the cursor to cut lines off; border sentinels fire at the player while a line is being built
a time limit on each level, with a bonus for clearing it in time
500+ levels in 9 worlds; any reached world can be chosen as a start point
notes: Macworld reviewed the Mac version on May 13, 2005 and credits Cornerstone TSP Games. Retro-replay lists Retro64 as developer and gives 2004. The cursor-tracking enemies, border shooters and missile/bomb/line-enhancer drops also appear in LaunchBox's description of Retro64's Windows game Cosmic Bugs (Nov 2004). The two are very likely one game under two names, but no source says so. The shorter line and inverted controls come only from retro-replay, an aggregator.

title: Jezzball Deluxe
mechanics: area-fill percentage goal (91% to win a round)
bouncing balls as hazards
picture reveal as area is claimed
lives
per-round time limit
points penalty/score counter
round-based progression (8 rounds in unregistered version)
multiple difficulty levels
notes: Windows shareware remake described by its archive.org listing as a 'remake of the Jezzball/Xonix games': the player reveals a colorful picture each level while avoiding moving balls, with several difficulty levels, effects and original music. The archived screenshot shows a fill-percentage HUD (FILL 0%, '91% FOR WIN'), ROUND, LIVES, a 1:30 TIME counter and POINTS, four bouncing balls in a bordered field, and an 'Unregistered version. 8 rounds only!' nag. It shipped on the Polish CyberMycha 05/2004 cover disc among shareware titles (alongside AirXonix and Alonix). A 'Jezzball Deluxe 1.0 PLUS 3 Trainer' also circulated, so version 1.0 preceded the archived v1.1. The screenshot does not show whether the player builds Jezzball-style splitting walls or draws Xonix-style trails. This is not the same game as 'Jezzball Classic Deluxe Edition' (Steam, 2025).

title: Styx Reloaded
mechanics: pickups for score, higher avatar speed and extra lives
notes: Wikipedia's Qix article (May 2008 revision) describes it as 'a 2004 freeware clone for Microsoft Windows' with 'a much better graphical presentation and smaller additions to game play, such as pickups for score, greater avatar speed, and extra lives'. The listing was later removed from the article.

title: Stix (2005)
notes: Straight clone: the author's BlitzMax remake of the Commodore 64 game Stix, a Qix port or clone, written in 2005 and later posted on itch.io; it runs on Windows 11, possibly after a DirectInput download. The same author made a separate PICO-8 'Stix' and a browser game 'Stix Disruption' with single-player and co-op modes (plus the Christmas-themed 'Stix Seasons').

title: Jezz Cubed
mechanics: 3D version: balls bounce inside a cube, and the player grows planes instead of lines to cut down its volume
notes: Billed as 'the first three-dimensional adaptation of JezzBall'. The Wikipedia stub was merged into JezzBall 'verbatim' on 13 June 2007, but the current JezzBall article no longer mentions it.

title: SINTOU 〜侵闘〜
developer: 神戸電子専門学校 (Kobe Denshi Senmon Gakko / Kobe Institute of Computing student project)
mechanics: 3D action: place blocks on the field to wall in ground and expand your territory
taller block stacks make sturdier walls
players hinder rival enclosures while expanding their own
LAN versus multiplayer
notes: Freeware student project, v1.00, archive dated 2007-08-01. Requires DirectX 9.0c and .NET Framework 1.1. A 3D versus territory game built on wall stacking rather than trail drawing.

title: Water Bugs
mechanics: each level has a different field shape instead of a fixed rectangle
new enemy types beyond those in Cosmic Bugs
a large set of power-ups
notes: The sequel to Cosmic Bugs, with an ocean theme, 3D-rendered graphics and digital sound. LaunchBox says it is inspired by JezzBall and Qix. The earlier entry's figures (599 levels, 9 missions, 13 enemy kinds, 12 power-ups, enemies roaming both boundary and field) came from StrategyWiki and VideoGameGeek. Both returned 403, so those figures were dropped as unverified.

title: YOUR GAME
mechanics: walking leaves a red floor trail that nobody, player or enemy, can walk on
enemies are killed by enclosing them in red floor with no gaps
enemies walk toward the player, so you lure them into dents in your trail, and several can be made to kill each other
turn-based: enemies move right after each player move
game over when the player is enclosed on all four sides
killing an enemy while another is still exploding chains a high-scoring combo
online score ranking, conditions that unlock new elements, and an ending
notes: HSP Program Contest 2023 entry. Vector carries v1.86+, dated 2024-06-12. Cursor keys only. A turn-based enclosure puzzle in which your own trail is both weapon and trap.

title: QEX64 (Excel VBA)
notes: Japanese freeware, a straight Qix clone written as an Excel VBA workbook. You move a marker on a field of square cells, avoid the line-shaped 'QEX' creature, and clear at 75% claimed. v1.9 file dated 2025-05-26; earlier versions may predate it.

title: Qix
alt_titles: Qix: The Computer Virus Game (1989 US computer-port marketing)
platforms: Atari 5200 (1982, ported by General Computer Corp., Atari)
Commodore 64 (1983 per Wikipedia; 1989 Taito version with Tim Follin music)
Fujitsu FM-7 (1983, Takara; see separate entry)
Amiga, Apple II, MS-DOS, Commodore 64/128 (1989, Alien Technology Group / Taito America)
Arcade: Space Invaders / Qix Silver Anniversary Edition 2-in-1 cabinet (2003)
PS2 (Taito Memories Gekan, Japan 2005, hidden title)
PS2, Xbox, Windows (Taito Legends 2, EU 2006, NA 2007)
PSP (Taito Memories Pocket, Japan 2006; Taito Legends Power-Up, NA 2007)
PSP (arcade Qix bundled in Qix++, Japan 2010)
Taito Egret II mini (2022, vertical play supported)
developer: Taito America (designed by Randy and Sandy Pfeiffer); Pixelated Arcade credits Threshold Research
mechanics: reference game: Fast Draw and Slow Draw buttons; areas closed entirely with Slow Draw fill red and score double, Fast Draw areas fill blue
stopping while drawing lights a Fuse that burns along the unfinished Stix toward the marker; trapping yourself also triggers it (the 'Spiral Death Trap')
the Qix wanders the open field without seeking the marker; touching the marker or the unfinished Stix costs a life
Sparx patrol the border and claimed edges but not unfinished Stix; a timer meter releases more Sparx and turns them into Super Sparx that can chase onto unfinished Stix
clear at 75% by default (adjustable between 50% and 90% in the settings); bonus for each 1% above the threshold
two Qix from level 3; splitting them into separate regions ends the level and raises a score multiplier by one per split, up to 9x, kept until a miss
1-2 players, alternating
notes: Base game, kept as the reference point. Port differences: the Atari 400/800 version uses one button (moving draws a normal line, pressing the button draws a red slow line), while the near arcade-perfect 5200 version needs a button press to start drawing (AtariProtos). The 1989 Taito America computer ports frame the Qix as a computer virus to 'immunize' the system against and call the Sparx 'sub-viruses'; an Amiga review reports that from level 7 the sub-viruses follow the marker while it draws. The FM-7 (auto-draw) and Game Boy (link play) ports have their own entries. The XBLA/PSP game Qix++ (Taito, 9 Dec 2009 XBLA, 25 Feb 2010 PSP Japan) is a separate game and should be its own entry.

title: Qix II: Tournament
mechanics: awards an extra life every time 90% or more of the field is enclosed (repeatable)
notes: Conversion of Qix with a new colour scheme and otherwise near-identical play. Wikipedia and arcade-history date it 1982; MAME and KLOV date the ROM set 1981.

title: Qix (FM-7)
developer: Unknown porter (original game by Taito America; Pixelated Arcade credits Threshold Research)
mechanics: no draw buttons: moving off the border into the field draws a Stix automatically, at close to arcade Fast Draw speed (so no Slow Draw choice)
stopping inside the field spawns the Fuse
the Sparx count rises every few stages and the Qix gradually gets smarter
clear at 75%
notes: Japanese home port on cassette. The manual adds a backstory: in 198X a bioweapon called QIX grows in a lab, and cursor robots spread chemicals along the walls to contain it. Because of an FM-series keyboard quirk, after a death the cursor keeps moving in the last key's direction, which costs new players several lives until they learn to press 5 to stop.

title: Super Qix
platforms: PS2 (Taito Memories II Joukan, Japan, 25 Jan 2007)
mechanics: 4-way lever and a single draw button: no Fast/Slow Draw choice
each of the 16 rounds hides a keyword picture that claimed territory reveals; completing it plays a celebration demo
the Qix is replaced by a Gremlin-like monster; Sparx still patrol the edges
pausing mid-line spawns a fire that creeps along the line toward the marker

enclosing areas randomly drops items: Barrier (blocks one hit), Harry (speed-up, two levels), Stop (briefly freezes enemies), Warp (skip to the next round), Extra (extra life), Double (two player markers at once)
letters can drop instead of items; spelling the round's keyword earns bonus points
clear at 75%; a Joker card appears whose character depends on the percentage claimed; 98% or more awards a free credit
16 rounds that loop; after game over you can continue from the current round
notes: Its hidden-picture engine is the basis of Kaneko's Gals Panic (1990). It stayed arcade-only until Taito Legends (2005). 1-2 players.

title: Volfied
alt_titles: SIMPLE1500 Vol.80 THE 陣取り ～ヴォルフィード1500～ (PlayStation, Japan)
platforms: PC Engine HuCard (Japan, 27 Dec 1989; port by I.T.L, published by Taito)
Mega Drive (Japan, 25 Jan 1991) / Genesis (North America, 1991, as Ultimate Qix); port by I.T.L, published by Taito
Amiga, Atari ST, Commodore 64, MS-DOS (1991, Empire Software)
ZX Spectrum (announced by Empire Software, never released)
PlayStation (Japan, 20 Dec 2001, D3 Publisher; North America, 1 Dec 2003, Mud Duck Productions, as Qix Neo)
Wii Virtual Console (Japan, 18 Nov 2008, PC Engine version)
au Smart Pass Premium Classic Games, browser (Japan, 7 Sep 2021)
Taito Egret II mini (2 Mar 2022, preinstalled)
PS4, Nintendo Switch (Arcade Archives by Hamster, 28 Mar 2024, OLD and NEW versions)
developer: Taito (designer Fukio Mitsuji); ports by I.T.L (PC Engine, Mega Drive), Empire Software (computers), Ving (FM Towns)
mechanics: one fixed draw speed (no slow/fast draw as in Qix); score depends only on area claimed; the ship can retrace its own unfinished line
no edge-patrolling Sparx: one boss per stage roams the open field with small minions; minions left on the claimed side are destroyed for bonus points
bosses have their own movement and projectile patterns (some pause, some fire spreads); some later stages reuse earlier bosses with upgrades
an enemy touching the unfinished line sends a spark along it toward the ship; the ship survives if it closes the area first
a shield blocks bullets while the ship is on the border, is down while drawing and drains over time; at zero, any enemy or bullet contact on the border kills
drawing for too long spawns a mine

item blocks pop in and out of existence and block movement; enclosing one while visible opens it: L laser (kills minions, not the boss), S speed (until stage clear or miss), C clears minions, P pauses shield drain, T freezes enemies, star special shot that can kill the boss (100,000 points for obtaining it)
clear by claiming 80% (the side holding the boss is 'outside'); the clear bonus rises toward 99.9%, up to 500,000
enclosing the boss with the very first line at 80% or more awards 1,000,000
the stage-6 boss is two parts; separating them so they cannot rejoin clears the stage (10,000, or 1,000,000 if claimed area is 1% or less)
hidden rule: leaving the enemies unable to move for a set time clears the stage regardless of claimed area (100,000)
claimed area shows the next stage's picture; 16 stages
PC Engine port: 40 rounds, 75% to clear, lines cannot be erased, sparks appear on completed lines instead of a mine, side HUD

Mega Drive port: widescreen field and three selectable rule modes: A (arcade rules), P (lines cannot be erased, item-block contents fixed), Q (lines cannot be erased, no items, separate fast-move button, original-Qix rules)
Ultimate Qix (US) per Sega Does: mode A uses the arcade spark rule under a stage timer; modes B and C kill instantly when an enemy touches the line; in C a button speeds the ship
Qix Neo / Volfied 1500 (PlayStation): Original (arcade) mode plus an Arrange mode of 96 levels with varying attack patterns; easy/normal/expert; top-5 ranking per mode
notes: Designed by Fukio Mitsuji (Bubble Bobble, Rainbow Islands); Japanese Wikipedia credits Taito's Central Research Institute and composer Hisayoshi Ogura. The arcade was Japan-only until Arcade Archives (2024). English Wikipedia places it in Taito Legends (2005), while Time Extension says Taito Legends 2. Empire's computer ports date from 1991, and only the C64 and DOS versions came out in North America. Famitsu gave the PC Engine version 30/40 (Silver Hall of Fame) and the Mega Drive version 26/40. Mega Drive Taizen says the Mega Drive plays closer to the arcade, since tricks such as enclosing the boss at once still work. Greatest Games calls the PC Engine port one of the most altered ports and says Qix Neo seems based on it. The Mega Drive rule modes show one engine tuned toward Qix or Volfied rules. The PC Engine ending reveals the pilot is a woman. Dropped as unverified: an AtGames Legends Arcade release, a Tec Toy Brazil release, an Amstrad CPC version, and 'enclosing every block yields a superweapon'. Greatest Games says box contents are randomised in the arcade.

title: Qix (Game Boy)
alt_titles: クイックス (ゲームボーイ)
platforms: Game Boy (JP 13 Apr 1990, NA May 1990, EU 28 Sep 1990)
mechanics: 2-player mode over the Game Link Cable, with the players presented as Team Mario and Team Luigi and a win or loss scene after each round
after a 1-player game, a Mario scene chosen by score thresholds (50,000 to 500,000) plays; the top scene shows Mario, Luigi, Peach and Toads
notes: It sold 1.15 million copies according to Japanese Wikipedia. It has its own entry because of the link-cable two-player mode. An Amiga reviewer calls it easier than the arcade.

title: Twin Qix
year: 1995 (prototype dated 17 Jan 1995; planned for May 1995, never released)
mechanics: 4-way lever and a single line button (labelled Draw Faster)
two players play at once on side-by-side fields, and each side reveals a different half of the level's background picture
versus mode: unlimited lives, the first to claim 95% wins the round, best of three
quota starts at 70% in round 1 and rises in later rounds; the 1-player run is 17 rounds
many new enemies and power-ups, including a statue
a boss-type enemy per round, with bosses and enemies reused later in the run
an enemy touching the trail while drawing is not an instant miss
notes: 2 players (not 4). The Japanese version used girl art by Izumi Takemoto, and a location-test version had a stripping variant. The overseas version shows world landmarks, ruins and aliens. A 2002 release on MediaKite's Net Gesen service was planned and then cancelled. A fan page says the main BGM was reused in Puzzle Bobble.

title: Qix Adventure
alt_titles: クイックスアドベンチャー
platforms: Game Boy Color (JP 22 Oct 1999, UK 15 Dec 2000)
developer: Coconuts Japan Entertainment (English version: Evolution Entertainment)
mechanics: Treasure mode: the treasure hunter Speedy travels a map whose areas hold different monsters
enclosing a monster captures it and releases treasure (chests on the playfield) to claim for items
captured monsters and treasures bring more opponents, bonus items and score multipliers; collected treasure decorates a room
monsters come with backstories; map progress depends on actions the game does not explain
Battle mode: two players on one Game Pak or over the Game Link Cable
Original mode with arcade Qix rules (75% to clear)
notes: A Game Boy Color game, not Game Boy Advance; no GBA Qix was found. Reviews were mediocre.

title: Qix 2000
mechanics: Game mode: faithful original Qix
Arrangement mode: claimed space reveals an anime-style girl illustration
Arrangement mode: psychedelic Qix graphics plus power-ups: speed-up (slow draw becomes fast, fast becomes faster) and speed-down (cancels it, punishing at normal speed)
clear threshold (default 75%) selectable among three settings
notes: Budget release in Success's SuperLite 1500 line; 1-2 players; vibration support.

title: Battle Qix
mechanics: battle mode: a strategic contest in which players compete to occupy more territory than the opponent and win coins
clearing levels rewards anime-style girl pictures
includes a remake of the original Qix
notes: 1-2 players, local. Arcade-history lists Battle Qix in the Qix series, but every release source has it as PlayStation-only.

title: QIX (Japanese mobile)
platforms: J-Phone Java (13 Mar 2002, 'Game selection' pack, 200 yen/month)
KDDI ezplus (25 Feb 2003, 'Taito Game Expo' pack, 300 yen/month)
mechanics: J-Phone version: clear at 75%; claiming the maximum 99% earns a special bonus
J-Phone version: each stage adds more Qix and makes them faster
notes: The ezplus release is billed as a faithful arcade recreation, including the Qix's stretching and contracting movement, so the changes above come from the J-Phone announcement only.

title: Space Invaders / Qix Silver Anniversary Edition
alt_titles: スペースインベーダー QIX
notes: A 25th-anniversary Space Invaders 2-in-1 cabinet containing colour Space Invaders and the original Qix, with cabinet art for both games. It is a re-release of Qix with no known gameplay changes and no interaction between the two games. The board runs an H8S CPU and an FPGA (MAME invqix).

title: Shakugan no Shana QIX
mechanics: claiming the set area in each stage unlocks that stage's character background image (Shana and others) in a CG viewing mode
notes: A licensed QIX tie-in listed under 携帯アプリ版（タイトー） ('mobile app versions (Taito)') in the Shakugan no Shana article; the article says to see QIX for the rules. The section's sibling apps shipped from Nov 2006 and Apr-May 2007 on i-appli (FOMA 903i), EZ-appli (BREW) and S!-appli. No date or carrier is given for the QIX title itself.

title: ONLINE QIX
alt_titles: オンラインクイックス
mechanics: real-time online 1v1 versus: one-button Quick Battle matchmaking, or join a friend's room
before a match each player picks a style or character, and each style sends a different attack to the opponent
single-player enemy roster grows from 3 (Qix, Fuse, Spark) to 10, with 7 new enemies that move unpredictably
items such as time stop and attacks on enemies
Collection Trophy long-term goals
notes: Billed as the first QIX with real-time online battles. Credited '©Bbmf ©TAITO CORP. 1981,2007'.

title: Retrocade
mechanics: licensed QIX is one cabinet in a multi-game Apple Arcade collection
classic goal: enclose at least 75% of the playfield while avoiding the Qix and Sparx
touch control schemes (buttons, joystick, swipe) plus Bluetooth controller support
collection-wide global leaderboards, per-game achievements, daily challenges and friend challenges
notes: An Apple Arcade collection whose titles include Asteroids, Bubble Bobble, Centipede, Dig Dug, Galaga, Pac-Man, Space Invaders, Tempest, Tetris and Qix. The Resolution Games page lists QIX as a 'Taito Classic'. According to the App Store version history, QIX was added in v1.13 on 26 Aug, which the copyright line and version sequence place in 2026.

title: 似非クイックス
mechanics: each stage uses a before/after image pair: claimed areas switch from the 'before' picture to the 'after' picture, and the site owner can supply any images

site owners embed it in their own web pages and set each stage through applet parameters: stage count, lives, goal % (1-99, default 75), Qix tail length, maximum Sparx count, Sparx spawn and speed-up intervals, game speed and colours
after a hit, the cursor blinks and is invulnerable to every enemy except the Qix while blinking
a fuse-like 'ignition' enemy appears on the line if you stall mid-cut, as in Qix
notes: The readme calls it a land-grab game that imitates Taito's QIX. Version history: 1.03 Sep 2003, 1.12 and 1.13 Oct 2003, 1.14 Jan 2005, 1.15 mid-Jan 2005. Vector's file qwixv115.zip is dated 2006-03-17. Controls: arrow keys or numeric keypad to move, Z or X held while moving to cut, Q to pause.

title: Qix (Flash, Drunk Men Work Here)
notes: A straight clone, 'very close to the original design' per Jay Is Games. Z draws fast Stix and X draws slow Stix (more points). Qix, Sparx and the Fuse are all present, and 75% clears the level. Jay Is Games reviewed it on Oct 20, 2004. The 2007 Wikipedia mirror links it as 'Qix emulator at DrunkMenWorkHere.org' (drunkmenworkhere.org/flash/qix2.swf).

title: 王子天蚕变
publisher: flashgame.co.kr; rehosted on 4399.com (uploaded by a 4399 user, 2007-01-05)
mechanics: draw only while holding Space; the line must return to your own area to close a region
claim 80% of the map within a time limit to advance
online high-score ranking that needs a flashgame.co.kr login (Korean UI strings in the SWF)
notes: The 4399 page (category 敏捷 'agility', listed 2007-01-05, marked suitable for ages 16+) sets up a little prince defending his country and says players of 写真天蚕变 (a Gals-Panic-style photo game) will find it easy. The SWF it serves credits '2006 www.flashgame.co.kr' and calls rank scripts under /flashrank/. Its ActionScript identifiers (picArr and mask, spider and webSet, mugi1Shoot, fire1-8, item1-5, timeStoper, bonus) hint at a picture reveal, a web-spinning spider, shooting enemies, item pickups and a time-stop item. These are unverified inferences from code names, not documented features.

title: Filler
mechanics: hold the mouse to grow a filler ball and release to freeze it; it also stops growing when it touches another filler ball
a bouncing ball running into a growing filler ball ends it, and collisions while growing cost lives
fill two-thirds of the level
limited lives and filler balls per level
a bouncing ball squashed by filler balls respawns in a top corner on the side away from where you are building
notes: Released on Kongregate 11 Jan 2008; last updated 1 Sep 2010. A JezzBall-adjacent fill game with growing circles in place of walls. The Qixote list has it under 'Closish Enough'.

title: xonixand 2.0
notes: Released on Kongregate on 19 May 2008, which tags it as Flash. The whole description is 'Variant of well-known game Xonix.' A player comment says the arrow keys move a pair of scissors. Other comments call it a plain Qix/Xonix clone. No documented change from Xonix.

title: Filler 2
mechanics: hold the mouse to grow a filler ball until it touches a bouncing ball or another filler, release to fix it in place
fill two thirds of the area to clear a level
a bouncing ball touching a still-growing filler costs a life
Normal difficulty: Space freezes the bouncing balls, draining a freeze meter
later levels add more balls and obstacles
three difficulties and 100 challenges
notes: Released 15 May 2009 on Kongregate (updated 12 Oct 2010). Sequel to SimianLogic's Filler (11 Jan 2008), with improved graphics and physics.

title: Fishonix
mechanics: inverted goal: cut away parts of a rectangular picture until less than 20% of the original remains
a cut-off part disappears only if no moving fish is inside it
the player is a fish steered with the arrow keys, and enemy fish can eat it (per player comments)
notes: Released on Kongregate on 19 Apr 2009. Its 'shrink to 20%' goal inverts the usual 75% capture target.

title: Kritter Krawler
platforms: Browser (Flash; Arkadium / Great Day Games, re-hosted on 4399.com in Dec 2011)
mechanics: player is a spider claiming area against a per-level percentage goal and a level timer
a main enemy with a timed transformation state
a laser enemy that telegraphs with a sonar pulse before firing a laser beam
saw enemies
power-ups that appear at intervals for a limited time and give bonus points
notes: The 4399 page (2011-12-20) says: arrow keys move the spider to enclose land; avoid dangers and enclose the area each level requires. The served SWF is Arkadium's ('com.arkadium.kritterkrawler', 'data/kritter-krawler_levelData.xml', Great Day Games branding), with build timestamps of Dec 15-17, 2009. 3 lives. The mechanics come from code identifiers (MainEnemy transform, LaserEnemy/LaserEnemySonar, SawEnemy, PowerUp with rate/time/points, _nTimeLeft, _nPercentGoal), not from a published description.

title: 圈地运动
mechanics: click to extend a growing line that claims ground; Space toggles its direction
three-pointed stars, gears and odd-shaped objects roam the field and must not touch the growing line
claim 80% of the field to advance
only five hits allowed for the whole run
notes: 4399 lists it under agility games, 0.68 MB, dated 2009-09-13. The footer says a 4399 user provided it, so the original author is unknown. 'Enclosure Movement' is a literal translation, not an official title.

title: Fill it! (Vvalter)
mechanics: hold the left mouse button to grow a white ball; it stops on release or when it hits a wall
a black bouncing ball touching your growing ball costs a life and destroys that ball
fill 66% of the field to clear
bigger balls score more
notes: Released 8 Sep 2010. The page calls it 'quite similar to the well known Filler Game'. It is separate from 11Sheep's 'Fillit'. The page does not state the technology.

title: Neo Xonix
mechanics: four enemy types: AntiXoni moves inside the field and cannot cross captured territory; Jumper jumps from side to side; Twins circle the field clockwise and counter-clockwise; Hunter chases the player everywhere
a life is lost on touching a creature, crossing your own trail, an AntiXoni crossing your trail, or the level timer running out
bonus S doubles speed; the Clock bonus freezes all creatures; other bonuses give points
need 75% to pass; extra life every 5,000 points
notes: Released on Kongregate on 30 Sep 2010 (updated 1 Nov 2010). The player character is 'Xoni', defending its world. The developer, Altarsoft, also made the catalogued Altarsoft Android Xonix; this Flash game may be an ancestor of that app.

title: Pac-Xon
year: by early 2010 (first release date unknown); HTML5 portal version dated Dec 2014
publisher: GameTop (Windows freeware download); many web portals host the browser version
mechanics: Pac-Man is the player and ghosts are the bouncing enemies
fill 75-80% of the board to advance (varies by version)
ghosts touching the player or the unfinished trail cost a life
ghosts can be captured by enclosing them with walls
fruit power-ups: cherries speed the player up, bananas slow the ghosts; some bonuses freeze the ghosts
later levels add faster ghosts, ghosts on straight paths, big ghosts, and enemies that eat finished walls
notes: A widely hosted Pac-Man/Xonix mashup. A Columbia University student project dated March 2010 already calls it 'the original PAC-XON game' (four lives, two ghosts at the start, 80% fill), so it predates 2010. Portal pages disagree on the fill threshold. Claims of a 2007 'Deluxe' edition, 20/50 level counts, an orb that lets you eat ghosts, and the trail disappearing after a death could not be verified and were removed. A Flash version was likely but not confirmed by the sources reached.

title: Reclamation
mechanics: enemies are a flocking swarm of insects that pour out of a trans-dimensional portal in the field; touching any insect or the portal destroys the ship
some insects follow the claimed edges, as Sparx do
a February 2010 update made the ship invincible on the edges, so only drawing is dangerous
sector (level) select from the menu
notes: Uploaded to Newgrounds on Jan 26, 2010 and front-paged Jan 29, 2010. The author describes it as 'inspired by Qix and Geometry Wars' (neon vector look, hypnotic soundtrack) and says it began as an experiment in swarming behaviour. Each sector needs a set percentage reclaimed. Re-hosted on 4399.com as 可怕的圈地 (Feb 2010), with an 'invincible' cheat build 可怕的圈地无敌版 (Nov 2011); see id 151.

title: Reclamation
alt_titles: 可怕的圈地无敌版 (invincible cheat build, 4399.com, 2011-11-11)
platforms: Browser (Flash; 4399.com re-upload of the Newgrounds/MochiAds game)
mechanics: enemies are a flocking swarm of insects that pour out of a trans-dimensional portal in the field; touching any insect or the portal destroys the ship
some insects follow the claimed edges, as Sparx do
a February 2010 update made the ship invincible on the edges, so only drawing is dangerous
sector (level) select from the menu
notes: DUPLICATE of id 150; merge. The 4399 page (uploaded 2010-02-25) describes 'controlling a small spaceship to enclose land while dodging monsters; enclose enough area to clear'. The SWF served by 4399 embeds the MochiAds game slug 'reclamation', so this is Globotix's Reclamation, not an original Chinese game. The 无敌版 page (2011-11-11) hosts a 6.09 MB build of the same size with invincibility.

title: 色球圈地
mechanics: click anywhere on the field to place a ball, and hold the button to keep it growing
a growing ball that touches the border or one of the bouncing small balls costs a life
each level gives a limited number of balls and lives; the level is cleared when the balls' combined area passes a target
notes: The portal calls it 'a territory-enclosing (圈地) game' and files it under agility games. Area-fill against bouncing balls, with a life lost when your growing shape is hit, follows JezzBall's rules, using growing circles instead of walls. It may be a localised copy of a Western Flash game; that could not be checked.

title: 3D天蚕变
mechanics: 3D-rendered field (AirXonix style): the player ball cuts parts off the field
crossing your own trail costs a life
an enemy ball that touches the player or crosses the open trail costs a life
enemies on two layers: several ball types in the open field and a separate star-like enemy on the claimed surface (from code class names)
bonus pickups; asset names point to extra life, slow, speed, extra time, warp, points and a harmful 'death' pickup
per-level percentage target under a time limit (level 1 asks for 60%)
notes: Uploaded to 4399 on 2011-06-29; the SWF metadata date is Jun 28, 2011. In-game credits: code and graphics by Ed 'ryzed' Ryzhov, music Massage/Sands, 'Inspired by AirXonix'. Tutorial text: 'Cut off parts of the field to finish the level. Don't cross your trail... Don't collide with the balls... If the ball crosses your trail you will lose life. Pick up bonuses.' The English release portal was not found.

title: Xonix 3d (myplayyard)
mechanics: 3D-rendered field whose camera does not always show the whole field (per a player comment)
crossing your own trail, or a ball touching it, costs a life at once
frequent bonus pickups
mines that appear at random spots (per a player comment)
a ball enemy that eats your trail back until it hits the border (per a player comment)
separate 2012 Levels pack with new levels
notes: Released on Kongregate on 27 Jun 2011; the Levels pack followed on 24 Sep 2012. A player comment says the credits read 'Inspired by AirXonix' and compares it with that game. It is a separate game from Delico Games' Android 'Xonix 3D'.

title: JezzPaul
mechanics: walling off JezzBall areas uncovers a hidden picture (always a cat in a sink)
Space switches the direction of the next line
notes: Released 13 Nov 2012. Adds a Gals Panic-style picture reveal to JezzBall. The page does not describe collision penalties, scoring or level progression.

title: Sloppy Ninja
mechanics: Space bar is a dedicated claim key: arrows move, Space claims area
double-tapping Space throws a shuriken, an attack on enemies (Destiny)
each level has its own enemy roster, with distinct abilities and special attacks
notes: The Demo (2013-02-22) and Fate (2013-03-22) pages say it is 'Based on classic arcade games like Qix and Volfied'. A third episode, Sloppy Ninja - Destiny, came out on 2015-02-14. Its page describes fighting savage monsters, with per-level enemies and a shuriken attack. The pages do not confirm the Flash runtime.

title: Xonix 3D 2
mechanics: drive a ball across the field to draw a line; the side cut off rises up in 3D as the capture
power-ups that switch the game into timed bonus states (per a player comment)
notes: Released on Kongregate on 26 Dec 2013. The description calls it 'a 3D take on the dice-em-up arcade avoidance of games like Fat Slice'. In a comment the developer promised a level pack with very large maps. The title suggests a sequel to myplayyard's 'Xonix 3d', but the developer account differs and no link is established.

title: Fezball
mechanics: mouse-only: click and hold to create a divider arrow, drag to aim it, release to start it
adds an easy mode the original lacked
clear 70% of the board (instead of JezzBall's 75%)
notes: Released 24 Aug 2014. A JezzBall remake with updated graphics.

title: Jezzball Jam
mechanics: Classic Mode: limited lives for the whole run; running out ends the game
Arcade Mode: lives set per level; running out costs your score but keeps you on the same level
right-click or Ctrl toggles horizontal or vertical lines; clear 75% to pass a level
a post-launch update lets the red and blue halves of a line start independently in some situations
tutorial
notes: Released 23 Jun 2014. Billed as a 'modern re-imagining of the classic Jezzball game from the early 90's'.

title: Space Cropper
mechanics: Player ship travels the border and cuts into space while the action key is held (Shift or J), tracing a dotted line. Y8 lists the controls as Move and Crop
20 levels. Levels 1-3 are a tutorial, and level 4 is the 'first mission in enemy territory'
Boss at level 10, and a final boss at level 20 (the Red Snake): it fires missiles in threes, and every third missile spawns a sentinel
Sentinels guard the map border, Sparx-style. A shield protects the player from them
Central turret that fires whenever the player leaves the border
Monster factories keep spawning enemies ('crabs') while they run
Neutral stones in the field can be used as cover against aggressive enemies
'Circler' balls orbit an object and pass over everything
Segment-follower monsters chase the player's trail
Pickups: shield, slow-game, point items, and a timed gift in the middle that vanishes after 20 seconds
About 17 monster classes in the code (bee, blue, green, red, metallic, confused metallic, canister, electric, factory, circler, followers, ship, tower and more)
notes: Newgrounds blocks automated fetches (403 'NG Guard'). I verified the game through its Y8 listing (added 13 Sep 2014: 'Cut off pieces of space as you blow up enemy ships & gather powerups to become stronger.') and through strings in the Y8-hosted SWF. The SWF metadata is dated 2014-08-25. It embeds the Newgrounds and Kongregate APIs and FGL ads. Its credits read 'DEVELOPMENT, ART & MUSIC: THOMAS JOHN', with a link to blog.open-design.be, and the ship and tile art is Daniel Cook's free Tyrian set (Lostgarden). The level tip strings confirm the per-level hazards listed in mechanics. The earlier claim of an '80% to clear' threshold could not be verified (the game shows a '% left' counter), so I dropped it. There is a sequel, Space Cropper 2 (Y8, added 18 Oct 2015), with the same credits. I could not run further web searches because the shared search budget was exhausted, and blog.open-design.be is not reachable from this sandbox.

title: QIX Spider Quest
mechanics: one hold-to-speed-up button (Space) in place of arcade Qix's separate fast/slow draw buttons
notes: Added to Kongregate on Apr 2, 2015, updated Apr 8, 2015. The description reads 'Remake of QIX, you're a spider bro and everything explodes.' The spider skin and heavy explosion effects are cosmetic. Kongregate rating 2.3.

title: PacXon New Realms
mechanics: 192 levels across 4 locations
4 to 6 unlockable character skins per location
fill at least 80% of the area to finish a level
arrow-key or swipe controls
notes: Billed as 'the long-awaited sequel to the 2007 classic PacXon Deluxe', with a revamped interface, a new soundtrack and pixel-art animations. GameDistribution distributes it (game id 727e29ac2f7a40e69a17dc7ff7f4c306), and pacxon.net embeds it. Its game files are dated 24 Jun 2024.

title: Cats Panic!
mechanics: cat-themed Gals Panic-style claiming, rated E (Everyone): draw a trail around territory to claim it while avoiding enemies
notes: The Newgrounds listing describes it as 'a puzzle game similar to Qix or Gal's Panic'. It is at version 1.1, scores 4.24/5 and had about 16.7k views. The icon timestamp is April 2026.

title: Claim (DaNuTree)
mechanics: guards have facing and visible vision cones (yellow when unaware, red once they spot you), chase only what they see, and search your last known position; pillars block sight
guard types: Wanderer (random), Hunter (narrow, longest cone, hunts you), Guardian (lurks deep in the open field), Nervous (wide short cone, twitchy) and Cutter (ignores you and cuts your trail)
touching your own trail or having it cut by a guard costs a life; 3 lives
the player can shoot in the facing direction: shoot guards for points, or shoot your own trail to blast an exit block at a score cost
from level 2: pillars that block you and guards, pits that stop only you, and a golden zone that pays triple; from level 4: roaming pillars that cut any line they cross
mystery orbs spin and then reveal a power-up (Speed, Shield, Freeze, Chain Guard, Rapid Fire, Spikes) or a power-down (Confuse, Fog, Alarm, Slow, Reinforcements, Drunk)
gadget chosen before each run, on a cooldown: Grapple Hook (pulls you two cells across open ground) or Smoke Bomb (invisible to guards for a few seconds)
after each level, pick one of three random upgrade cards that last the rest of the run
after claiming 75% you may cash out at any time or push on for a growing risk bonus that one catch wipes out
modes: Normal, Chaos (orbs everywhere) and Zen (guards stand still); cameras: fixed, follow, and mirrored-control
notes: A stealth-and-roguelite take on Qix/Xonix. The push-your-luck cash-out after 75% stands out. Released on itch.io about the end of Aug 2026 (page says '70 days ago' on 9 Nov 2026). Has a 12-step tutorial with no life cost, per-mode high scores and achievements. Marked AI-assisted for code, graphics, sounds and text.

title: Containment (hau-game-studio)
mechanics: click and drag a horizontal or vertical barrier that grows across open space
one hit: an anomaly touching an unfinished barrier ends the whole run
capture 75% to clear a wave; endless waves with more and faster anomalies
visual theme changes every five cleared waves
local personal-best tracking with fast restarts
notes: Published on itch.io on 10 Oct 2026, free, mouse-only. It is separate from mikezupper's 'Containment' already in the catalog.

title: Glimmer: Capture the Light
mechanics: each captured piece reveals part of a hidden painting (non-adult picture reveal): 60 paintings across 6 worlds
lure shadow enemies into Supernova traps
weekly leagues
asynchronous ghost challenges: friends race your recorded ghost
swipe controls on touch screens (arrows/WASD on PC)
notes: Game Jolt page published Nov 8, 2026. Free; the player steers a little flame through darkness and closes the trail to capture.

title: Neon Xonix
mechanics: claim 80% or more of the board
bouncing enemies
touch and keyboard controls with adjustable settings
notes: Neon-styled Xonix. Published on Game Jolt on 3 Oct 2026; the itch.io page was updated on 22 Oct 2026. The full version is hosted at neon-xonix-20.vercel.app and can be installed as a PWA. itch.io marks it 'No generative AI was used'.

title: Territory Action
platforms: Browser (HTML5; PC with keyboard, smartphones not supported)
developer: Torai Games (programming assisted by OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT)
notes: A straight clone: hold Space while moving off the border to draw, connect the line to another border to claim, an enemy touching you mid-line is a miss, and 75% clears the stage. The Japanese description calls it a 陣取りアクションゲーム (genre term, not a title). The itch.io page gives no publish date; its game id (4851520) falls between pages from May 2025 and October 2026, suggesting roughly mid-2026.

title: Territory Arrow
mechanics: one-button control: hold to move the arrow along a glowing closed shape, release to stop
the trail carved by the arrow claims territory; fill 90% before the timer runs out or rivals get there first
hazards: pink gears end the run on contact, and red enemy arrows hunt you
twin linked arrows move in lockstep, so you must plot a path that avoids a collision
non-rectangular fields: squares, locks, stars and winding curves
notes: Free browser game for landscape screens on phone and desktop. The itch.io page showed 'Published 25 days ago' on 2026-11-09, so it came out around mid-October 2026. The page does not say whether the twin linked arrows are enemies or player-controlled.

title: VoidCutter
mechanics: each capture restores part of a Turkish landmark (Cappadocia, Pamukkale, Ephesus, Hagia Sophia, Mount Nemrut) hidden under the Void
enemy roster of Drifting Shadows, Border Followers (Sparx analog) and Hunters, plus a mechanical phoenix boss guarding the final level
Time Fracture: spend charged Void Energy to slow everything down
up to three stars per level for bonus goals
Daily Map: one shared layout per day for every player
mouse-drag, swipe and on-screen D-pad controls
notes: Published on itch.io Oct 18, 2026; free. The itch.io page discloses AI assistance for code, graphics and text.

title: Xonix Wars Territory Capture
mechanics: the player is a tank; enemies include drones, jets, flying mines, missiles and heavy bombers
some enemies track the tank and destroy it by hitting its trail
driving back along your own trail is allowed with no penalty
capture 80% of the map to win; capturing over 90% gives an extra life
5 war zones, with progress saved after each completed stage
notes: Free military-themed Xonix in which retracing your own trail is safe. Published on itch.io about 8 Nov 2026 (page says '1 day ago'). Made with Construct; the tags say Construct 2 and the tools list says Construct 3. Marked AI-assisted, with AI text-to-speech soldier voices.

title: Quick Paper Game
mechanics: glide across the board leaving a trail and close the loop to claim territory
closing a loop over opponents' land steals it; getting hit while drawing ends the run
notes: Paper.io-style browser game with a paper art style; the page does not name Paper.io. Free; publish date not shown.
